title.zh: 卷四百七十二 列傳第二百三十一 姦臣二 蔡京弟:卞 子:攸 翛 族子:崈 趙良嗣 張覺 郭藥師
title.en: Volume 472 Biographies 231: Treacherous Officials 2 - Cai Jing and younger brother: Bian, sons: You, Shu, descendant: Chong, Zhao Liangsi, Zhang Jue, Guo Yaoshi
title.raw: 卷四百七十二 列傳第二百三十一 姦臣二 蔡京弟:卞 子:攸 翛 族子:崈 趙良嗣 張覺 郭藥師 Volume 472 Biographies 231: Treacherous Officials 2 - Cai Jing and younger brother: Bian, sons: You, Shu, descendant: Chong, Zhao Liangsi, Zhang Jue, Guo Yaoshi

sentences.zh: 蔡京弟:卞 子:攸 翛 族子:崈 趙良嗣附:張覺 郭藥師

translations.literal: Cai Jing, younger brother: Bian, sons: You, Shu, clansman: Chong, Zhao Liangsi appended: Zhang Jue, Guo Yaoshi
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing; younger brother, Bian; sons, You and Shu; clansman, Chong; with appended biographies of Zhao Liangsi, Zhang Jue, and Guo Yaoshi

sentences.zh: 蔡京字元長，興化仙遊人。

translations.literal: Cai Jing, styled Yuanchang, was a man of Xianyou in Xinghua.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing, whose style name was Yuanchang, came from Xianyou in Xinghua prefecture.

sentences.zh: 登熙甯三年進士第，調錢塘尉、舒州推官，累遷起居郎。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Xiuning, was assigned as Qiantang sheriff and Shuzhou judicial reviewer, and was repeatedly promoted to Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the third year of the Xiuning era, served as sheriff of Qiantang and judicial reviewer in Shuzhou, and rose through several posts to Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 使遼還，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: On returning from an embassy to Liao, he was appointed Central Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from a mission to the Liao, he was appointed a drafter in the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時弟卞已為舍人，故事，入官以先後為序，卞乞班京下。

translations.literal: At the time his younger brother Bian was already a drafter; by precedent those entering office were ordered by seniority, and Bian requested to rank below Jing.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Bian was already a drafter. By custom, colleagues entering office were ranked by seniority, but Bian asked to be placed below Jing.

sentences.zh: 兄弟同掌書命，朝廷榮之。

translations.literal: The brothers together held charge of imperial documents, and the court honored them.
translations.idiomatic: The two brothers jointly controlled imperial drafting, and the court regarded it as a mark of honor.

sentences.zh: 改龍圖閣待制、知開封府。

translations.literal: He was changed to Dragon Diagram Hall Attendant Drafter and made prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Attendant Drafter in the Dragon Diagram Hall and appointed prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 元豐末，大臣議所立，京附蔡確，將害王珪以貪定策之功，不克。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanfeng, when great ministers debated whom to install, Jing attached himself to Cai Que and intended to harm Wang Gui in order to seize the merit of fixing the succession, but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Yuanfeng era, as senior ministers debated the succession, Jing sided with Cai Que and tried to destroy Wang Gui so he could claim credit for settling the question, but failed.

sentences.zh: 司馬光秉政，復差役法，為期五日，同列病太迫，京獨如約，悉改畿縣雇役，無一違者。

translations.literal: When Sima Guang held power, he restored the corvée-and-service law with a five-day deadline; colleagues complained it was too pressing, but Jing alone kept the appointment, changing hired service throughout the metropolitan counties without a single violation.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Guang took power and revived the corvée system, he set a five-day deadline. His colleagues protested that it was too harsh, but Jing alone met the deadline and converted hired service in every metropolitan county without exception.

sentences.zh: 詣政事堂白光，光喜曰：「使人人奉法如君，何不可行之有！

translations.literal: He went to the Secretariat to report to Guang; Guang said with pleasure, "If everyone obeyed the law as you do, how could it not be carried out!"
translations.idiomatic: He went to the Secretariat to report to Guang, who said delightedly, "If everyone obeyed the law as you do, how could the policy fail?"

sentences.zh: 」已而台諫言京挾邪壞法，出知成德軍，改瀛州，徙成都。

translations.literal: " Shortly afterward the censorate and remonstrance officials said Jing harbored perversity and ruined the law; he was sent out to govern Chengde Army, then changed to Yingzhou, and transferred to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward censors charged that Jing was devious and was undermining the law. He was sent out to govern Chengde, then reassigned to Yingzhou and later transferred to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 諫官范祖禹論京不可用，乃改江、淮、荊、浙發運使，又改知揚州。

translations.literal: The remonstrance official Fan Zuyu argued that Jing should not be used; he was then changed to Transport Commissioner for the Jiang, Huai, Jing, and Zhe circuits, and again changed to prefect of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The remonstrator Fan Zuyu argued that Jing should not be employed, so he was made transport commissioner for the Jiang-Huai-Jing-Zhe region and later prefect of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 曆鄆、永興軍，遷龍圖閣直學士，復知成都。

translations.literal: He served in Yun and Yongxing Army, was promoted to Dragon Diagram Hall Academician Expositor, and again governed Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He served in Yun prefecture and Yongxing, was promoted to expositor academician in the Dragon Diagram Hall, and again governed Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，入權戶部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaosheng he entered the capital as acting Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shaosheng era he returned to the capital as acting Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 章惇復變役法，置司講議，久不決。

translations.literal: Zhang Dun again changed the service law and established an office for discussion; for a long time no decision was reached.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun sought again to change the service law and set up a deliberation office, but debate dragged on without resolution.

sentences.zh: 京謂惇曰：「取熙甯成法施行之爾，何以講為？

translations.literal: Jing said to Dun, "Just take the completed laws of Xiuning and put them into effect—why discuss?"
translations.idiomatic: Jing told Dun, "Simply take the finished Xiuning statutes and enforce them. What is there to debate?"

sentences.zh: 」惇然之，雇役遂定。

translations.literal: " Dun approved this, and hired service was thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: " Dun agreed, and the hired-service system was settled at last.

sentences.zh: 差雇兩法，光、惇不同。

translations.literal: Between the corvée and hired-service systems, Guang and Dun differed.
translations.idiomatic: Guang and Dun had stood on opposite sides of the corvée and hired-service laws.

sentences.zh: 十年間京再蒞其事，成於反掌，兩人相倚以濟，識者有以見其奸。

translations.literal: Within ten years Jing again took charge of the matter and accomplished it as easily as turning the hand; the two men relied on each other to succeed, and those who understood could see their treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Within a decade Jing took up the matter again and finished it with ease. The two men leaned on each other to get their way, and perceptive observers could already see their duplicity.

sentences.zh: 卞拜右丞，以京為翰林學士兼侍讀，修國史。

translations.literal: Bian was appointed Right Vice Director; Jing was made Hanlin Academician and concurrent Lecturer-in-Waiting, compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: When Bian became Right Vice Director, Jing was made a Hanlin academician, concurrent imperial reader, and compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 文及甫獄起，命京窮治，京捕內侍張士良，令述陳衍事狀，即以大逆不道論誅，並劉摯、梁燾劾之。

translations.literal: When the Wen Jifu case arose, Jing was ordered to investigate thoroughly; Jing arrested the inner attendant Zhang Shiliang, made him narrate Chen Yan's circumstances, and at once sentenced them to execution for great treason, also impeaching Liu Zhi and Liang Tao.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wen Jifu affair broke out, Jing was ordered to pursue it to the end. He arrested the inner attendant Zhang Shiliang, forced him to recount Chen Yan's actions, and immediately secured convictions for treason, while also impeaching Liu Zhi and Liang Tao.

sentences.zh: 衍死，二人亦貶死，皆錮其子孫。

translations.literal: Yan died, and the two men also died in exile; all their descendants were barred from office.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was executed, and the other two died in exile as well. Their descendants were all barred from office.

sentences.zh: 王岩叟、范祖禹、劉安世復遠竄。

translations.literal: Wang Yansou, Fan Zuyu, and Liu Anshi were again exiled far away.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yansou, Fan Zuyu, and Liu Anshi were banished even farther away.

sentences.zh: 京覬執政，曾布知樞密院，忌之，密言卞備位承轄，京不可以同升，但進承旨。

translations.literal: Jing coveted the chief ministership; Zeng Bu, knowing the Bureau of Military Affairs, envied him and secretly said Bian already held a supporting post, so Jing could not rise together with him but should only be advanced to Hanlin Academician-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Jing coveted real power in government. Zeng Bu, who controlled the Bureau of Military Affairs, resented him and secretly argued that with Bian already in a supporting post, Jing should not be promoted alongside him but only to Hanlin Academician-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 童貫以供奉官詣三吳訪書畫奇巧，留杭累月，京與遊，不舍晝夜。

translations.literal: Tong Guan, as a palace supply officer, went to the Three Wu region to seek rare books, paintings, and curiosities; he stayed in Hangzhou for many months, and Jing kept company with him day and night without leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Guan went to the lower Yangzi region as a palace supply officer to hunt for rare books, paintings, and curios. He stayed in Hangzhou for months, and Jing kept him company day and night.

sentences.zh: 凡所畫屏幛、扇帶之屬，貫日以達禁中，且附語言論奏至帝所，由是帝屬意京。

translations.literal: Whatever painted screens, fans, belts, and the like there were, Guan daily sent them into the forbidden precincts, and also attached words so that memorials reached the emperor; thereby the emperor fixed his attention on Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Every day Guan sent painted screens, fans, belts, and the like into the palace, along with messages that carried Jing's views to the emperor. From this the emperor began to favor Jing.

sentences.zh: 又太學博士范致虛素與左街道錄徐知常善，知常以符水出入元符後殿，致虛深結之，道其平日趣向，謂非相京不足以有為。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Imperial University erudite Fan Zhixu had long been friendly with the Left Avenue registrar Xu Zhichang; Zhichang used talisman water to enter and leave the Yuanfu Rear Hall, and Zhixu formed a deep bond with him, speaking of Jing's usual inclinations and saying that unless Jing became chief minister nothing could be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial University erudite Fan Zhixu was also close to Xu Zhichang, registrar of the Left Avenue, who used ritual water to enter the Yuanfu Rear Hall. Fan cultivated him deeply and told him of Jing's ambitions, saying that nothing important could be done unless Jing became chief minister.

sentences.zh: 已而宮妾、宦官合為一詞譽京，遂擢致虛右正言，起京知定州。

translations.literal: Before long palace women and eunuchs united in one voice to praise Jing; Zhixu was then promoted to Right Remonstrator, and Jing was recalled to govern Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon palace women and eunuchs were all praising Jing in one voice. Fan Zhixu was promoted to Right Remonstrator, and Jing was recalled to govern Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 崇甯元年，徙大名府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongning he was transferred to Daming prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongning he was transferred to Daming.

sentences.zh: 韓忠彥與曾布交惡，謀引京自助，復用為學士承旨。

translations.literal: Han Zhongyan and Zeng Bu were mutually hostile; they plotted to bring in Jing to assist themselves, and he was again used as Hanlin Academician-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Han Zhongyan and Zeng Bu were at odds and plotted to bring Jing in as an ally. He was again appointed Hanlin Academician-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 徽宗有意修熙、豐政事，起居舍人鄧洵武黨京，撰《愛莫助之圖》以獻，徽宗遂決意用京。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong intended to restore Xi and Feng policies; the Attendant Gentleman Deng Xunwu joined Jing's faction, composed the "Chart of None Able to Help" and presented it, and Huizong then resolved to employ Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong wished to revive the policies of the Xi and Feng eras. Deng Xunwu, an attendant gentleman, sided with Jing and presented a chart titled "No One Can Help" to show how few allies the reformers still had. Huizong then decided to use Jing.

sentences.zh: 忠彥罷，拜尚書左丞，俄代曾布為右僕射。

translations.literal: Zhongyan was dismissed; Jing was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and soon replaced Zeng Bu as Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongyan was dismissed, Jing was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and soon replaced Zeng Bu as Right Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 制下之日，賜坐延和殿，命之曰：「神宗創法立制，先帝繼之，兩遭變更，國是未定。

translations.literal: On the day the appointment was issued, he was granted a seat in the Yanhe Hall and commanded: "Shenzong created laws and established institutions; the late emperor continued them. Twice they were altered, and the national policy is not settled."
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his appointment he was given a seat in the Yanhe Hall. The emperor told him, "Shenzong created new laws and institutions, and my father continued them, yet they were overturned twice and the state's course remains unsettled."

sentences.zh: 朕欲上述父兄之志，卿何以教之？

translations.literal: I wish to carry upward the aims of father and elder brother—how will you instruct me?"
translations.idiomatic: I wish to carry out the aims of my father and grandfather. What counsel do you have for me?"

sentences.zh: 」京頓首謝，願盡死。

translations.literal: " Jing bowed his head in thanks and vowed to exhaust himself unto death.
translations.idiomatic: " Jing kowtowed and pledged to serve unto death.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，進左僕射。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year he was advanced to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year he was promoted to Left Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 京起於逐臣，一旦得志，天下拭目所為，而京陰托「紹述」之柄，箝制天子，用條例司故事，即都省置講議司，自為提舉，以其党吳居厚、王漢之十余人為僚屬，取政事之大者，如宗室、冗官、國用、商旅、鹽澤、賦調、尹牧，每一事以三人主之。

translations.literal: Jing rose from a banished subject; once he gained his ambition the realm watched what he would do, while Jing secretly seized the handle of "continuing the legacy," shackled the Son of Heaven, used the precedent of the Regulations Office, and at the Metropolitan Secretariat established a Deliberation Office with himself as superintendent, making more than ten of his faction such as Wu Juho and Wang Hanzhi staff members; he took great affairs of government such as the imperial clan, redundant offices, state expenditure, merchants and travelers, salt marshes, tax levies, and prefectural administration, and for each matter assigned three men to direct it.
translations.idiomatic: Jing had risen from exile, and once he gained power the whole realm watched what he would do. In secret he seized the slogan of "continuing the legacy," constrained the emperor, and, following the old Regulations Office model, set up a Deliberation Office at the Metropolitan Secretariat with himself as superintendent. More than ten allies, including Wu Juho and Wang Hanzhi, served on its staff. Major areas of policy—the imperial clan, redundant offices, state finances, commerce, salt administration, taxation, and local government—were each placed under a trio of directors.

sentences.zh: 凡所設施，皆由是出。

translations.literal: Whatever was instituted all issued from this.
translations.idiomatic: Every measure he introduced came out of that office.

sentences.zh: 用馮澥、钱遹之議，復廢元祐皇后。

translations.literal: Using the proposals of Feng Xi and Qian Yuzhi, he again deposed the Yuanyou empress.
translations.idiomatic: Following proposals by Feng Xi and Qian Yuzhi, he again deposed the Yuanyou empress.

sentences.zh: 罷科舉法，令州縣悉仿太學三舍考選，建辟雍外學于城南，以待四方之士。

translations.literal: He abolished the examination system, ordered all prefectures and counties to imitate the Imperial University's three-college examination selection, and built an outer Imperial College at the southern wall of the city to await scholars from all directions.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished the civil service examinations and ordered every prefecture and county to adopt the Imperial University's three-college selection system. An outer college was built south of the capital to receive scholars from across the realm.

sentences.zh: 推方田於天下。

translations.literal: He extended the square-field system throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He extended the square-field land survey across the empire.

sentences.zh: 榷江、淮七路茶，官自為市。

translations.literal: He monopolized tea in the seven circuits of Jiang and Huai, with the state itself as merchant.
translations.idiomatic: He imposed a state tea monopoly over seven circuits in the Jiang-Huai region, with the government itself acting as trader.

sentences.zh: 盡更鹽鈔法，凡舊鈔皆弗用，富商巨賈嘗齎持數十萬緡，一旦化為流丐，甚者至赴水及縊死。

translations.literal: He completely changed the salt certificate law; all old certificates were not used. Great merchants who had once carried hundreds of thousands of strings suddenly became vagrant beggars; some even threw themselves into water or hanged themselves to death.
translations.idiomatic: He overhauled the salt certificate system and voided every old certificate. Wealthy merchants who had held certificates worth hundreds of thousands of strings were ruined overnight; some drowned themselves or hanged themselves in despair.

sentences.zh: 提點淮東刑獄章糸宰見而哀之，奏改法誤民，京怒，奪其官。

translations.literal: The Huaidong judicial intendant Zhang Zai saw this and pitied them; he memorialized that the changed law harmed the people. Jing was angry and stripped him of office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zai, judicial intendant of Huaidong, saw their suffering and memorialized that the new law was harming the people. Jing was furious and stripped him of his post.

sentences.zh: 因鑄當十大錢，盡陷糸宰諸弟。

translations.literal: He then cast ten-cash large coins and implicated all of Zai's younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He then minted ten-cash coins and used the case to implicate all of Zhang Zai's younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 御史沈畸等用治獄失意，羈削者六人。

translations.literal: The censor Shen Ji and others, because they were displeased in handling cases, had six men detained and demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Because censors such as Shen Ji displeased him in handling legal cases, six of them were detained and demoted.

sentences.zh: 陳瓘子正匯以上書黥置海島。

translations.literal: Chen Guan's son Chen Zhenghui, for submitting a memorial, was tattooed and exiled to a sea island.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhenghui, son of Chen Guan, was tattooed and exiled to a coastal island for submitting a memorial.

sentences.zh: 南開黔中，築靖州。

translations.literal: To the south he opened Qianzhong and built Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the south he opened Qianzhong and built Jing prefecture.

sentences.zh: 辰溪徭叛，殺漵浦令，京重為賞，募殺一首領者賜之絹三百，官以班行，且不令質究本末。

translations.literal: The Yao of Chenxi rebelled and killed the Xupu magistrate; Jing made the rewards heavy, recruiting killers of a single leader with a gift of three hundred bolts of silk and office by roster rank, and moreover did not allow investigation of the rights and wrongs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yao of Chenxi rebelled and killed the magistrate of Xupu, Jing offered rich rewards: three hundred bolts of silk and an official rank to anyone who killed a tribal leader, without requiring proof of who had actually rebelled.

sentences.zh: 荊南守馬马珹言：「有生徭，有省地徭，今未知叛者為何種族，若計級行賞，俱不能無枉濫。

translations.literal: The Jingnan prefect Ma Maqi said: "There are native Yao and Yao on provincial land; now it is not known which tribe the rebels belong to. If rewards are given by head count, both cannot be without wrongful killing."
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Jingnan, Ma Qi, said, "There are native Yao and Yao living on provincial lands. We do not even know which group has rebelled. If rewards are handed out by the head, innocent people are bound to be killed."

sentences.zh: 」蔣之奇知樞密院，恐忤京意，白言珹不體國，京罷珹，命舒亶代之，以剿無群徭為期。

translations.literal: " Jiang Zhiqi, knowing the Bureau of Military Affairs, feared to offend Jing's intent and reported that Qi did not consider the state; Jing dismissed Qi and ordered Shu Dan to replace him, setting as the deadline the extermination of all Yao bands.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiang Zhiqi, who controlled the Bureau of Military Affairs, feared to cross Jing and reported that Ma Qi was disloyal to the state. Jing dismissed Ma Qi and sent Shu Dan in his place with orders to exterminate every Yao band.

sentences.zh: 西收湟川、鄯、廓，取牱、夜郎地。

translations.literal: To the west he recovered Huangchuan, Shan, and Kuo, and took the lands of Zangke and Yelang.
translations.idiomatic: In the west he recovered Huangchuan, Shan, and Kuo and seized the territories of Zangke and Yelang.

sentences.zh: 擢童貫領節度使，其後揚戩、藍從熙、譚稹、梁師成皆踵之。

translations.literal: He promoted Tong Guan to lead as military commissioner; afterward Yang Jian, Lan Congxi, Tan Zhen, and Liang Shicheng all followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted Tong Guan to a frontier military commissionership, and afterward Yang Jian, Lan Congxi, Tan Zhen, and Liang Shicheng followed the same path.

sentences.zh: 凡寄資一切轉行，祖宗之法蕩然無餘矣。

translations.literal: Whatever provisional qualifications were all converted in succession; the laws of the ancestors were swept away without remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Every provisional appointment was converted into a regular post, until the institutions of the founding emperors had been swept away entirely.

sentences.zh: 又欲兵柄士心皆歸己，建澶、鄭、曹、拱州為四輔，各屯兵二萬，而用其姻昵宋喬年、胡師文為郡守。

translations.literal: He also wished that military authority and the hearts of officers all return to himself; he made Chan, Zheng, Cao, and Gong prefectures the Four Supports, each garrisoning twenty thousand troops, and used his in-laws Song Qiaonian and Hu Shiwen as prefects.
translations.idiomatic: He also wanted military power and the loyalty of the officer corps concentrated in his hands. He made Chan, Zheng, Cao, and Gong the Four Supporting prefectures, each with a garrison of twenty thousand men, and appointed his relatives Song Qiaonian and Hu Shiwen as their prefects.

sentences.zh: 禁卒幹扌取月給錢五百，驟增十倍以固結之。

translations.literal: Palace guards who sought the monthly stipend of five hundred cash had it suddenly increased tenfold to bind them firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Palace guards who had been pressing for a monthly stipend of five hundred cash suddenly had it raised tenfold to secure their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 威福在手，中外莫敢議。

translations.literal: With authority and favor in his hands, inside and outside none dared discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: With power and favor firmly in his grasp, no one inside or outside the court dared criticize him.

sentences.zh: 累轉司空，封嘉國公。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Minister of Works and enfeoffed as Duke of Jia.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to Minister of Works and was enfeoffed as Duke of Jia.

sentences.zh: 京既貴而貪益甚，已受僕射奉，復創取司空寄祿錢，如粟、豆、柴薪與亻兼從糧賜如故，時皆折支，亦悉從真給，但入熟狀奏行，帝不知也。

translations.literal: Once Jing was exalted his greed grew still greater; having already received the Vice Director's salary, he again newly took the Minister of Works nominal salary, and grain, beans, firewood, and attendant grain allowances as before; at the time all were paid in commutation, yet he also had everything paid in full, only entering a routine memorial for approval—the emperor did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Once elevated, Jing grew greedier still. He already drew a grand councilor's salary, yet also claimed the nominal stipend of Minister of Works along with grain, beans, firewood, and attendant rations as before. Although such payments were usually commuted to cash, he insisted on receiving them in kind. He merely filed routine approval memorials, and the emperor never knew.

sentences.zh: 時元祐群臣貶竄死徙略盡，京猶未愜意，命等其罪狀，首以司馬光，目曰奸党，刻石文德殿門，又自書為大碑，遍班郡國。

translations.literal: At the time the Yuanyou ministers had been banished, exiled, died, or transferred until nearly all were gone; Jing was still not satisfied, ordered their crimes ranked, put Sima Guang first, labeled them the Treacherous Faction, carved it in stone at the Wende Hall gate, and also personally wrote a great stele distributed throughout prefectures and states.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Yuanyou ministers had been exiled, demoted, or killed until almost none remained, yet Jing was still unsatisfied. He ordered their offenses ranked, placed Sima Guang at the head, and labeled them the Treacherous Faction. The list was carved in stone at the gate of the Wende Hall, and Jing himself wrote a great stele that was sent to every prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，元符末以日食求言，言者多及熙寧、紹聖之政，則又籍範柔中以下為邪等凡名在兩籍者三百九人，皆錮其子孫，不得官京師及近甸。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the end of Yuanfu, because of an eclipse the court sought opinions; many opinions touched Xiuning and Shaosheng policies, so he also registered Fan Rouzhong and below as an evil grade; in all those named on the two registers were 309 persons, all barred in their descendants from office in the capital and nearby domains.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after an eclipse at the end of the Yuanfu era, the court had solicited opinions, and many memorials had defended the policies of Xiuning and Shaosheng. Jing then registered Fan Rouzhong and others as a second list of malign officials. In all, 309 men on the two lists had their descendants barred from office in the capital and its vicinity.

sentences.zh: 五年，進司空、開府儀同三司、安遠軍節度使，改封魏國。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was advanced to Minister of Works, Defender-in-Chief with ceremony equal to the Three Dukes, and military commissioner of Anyuan Army, and changed enfeoffment to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to Minister of Works, Defender-in-Chief with Three-Duke honors, and military commissioner of Anyuan, and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 時承平既久，帑庾盈溢，京倡為豐、亨、豫、大之說，視官爵財物如糞土，累朝所儲掃地矣。

translations.literal: At the time peace had long continued and the treasuries overflowed; Jing advocated the doctrine of Abundance, Success, Ease, and Greatness, treating offices, titles, and wealth like dung and soil, and what successive courts had stored was swept clean.
translations.idiomatic: Peace had lasted so long that the treasuries overflowed. Jing preached the doctrine of Abundance, Success, Ease, and Greatness, treating offices and wealth like dirt, and the savings of many reigns were squandered.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗大宴，出玉琖、玉卮示輔臣曰：「欲用此，恐人以為太華。

translations.literal: The emperor once held a great banquet, brought out jade bowls and jade goblets to show the chief ministers, and said, "I wish to use these, but fear people will think it too lavish."
translations.idiomatic: At one grand banquet the emperor brought out jade bowls and goblets and told his chief ministers, "I would like to use these, but I fear people will say it is too extravagant."

sentences.zh: 」京曰：「臣昔使契丹，見玉盤琖，皆石晉時物，持以誇臣，謂南朝無此。

translations.literal: " Jing said, "When your servant formerly went on mission to the Khitan, I saw jade plates and bowls, all objects from the Shi Jin period; they held them up to boast to your servant, saying the Southern Court had nothing like this."
translations.idiomatic: " Jing replied, "When I was envoy to the Khitan, they showed me jade plates and bowls from the Later Jin and boasted that the Song had nothing like them."

sentences.zh: 今用之上壽，於禮無嫌。

translations.literal: To use them now for the longevity toast is without impropriety in ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Using them now for a longevity toast would be perfectly proper.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「先帝作一小台財數尺，上封者甚眾，朕甚畏其言。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "The late emperor built a small terrace costing several feet of timber, and memorials of remonstrance were very numerous; I greatly fear such words."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "My father built a small terrace that cost only a few feet of timber, yet he was flooded with remonstrances. I am very afraid of such criticism."

sentences.zh: 此器已就久矣，倘人言復興，久當莫辨。

translations.literal: These vessels have long been completed; if people's talk rises again, in time it will no longer be distinguishable.
translations.idiomatic: These vessels have been finished for a long time. If criticism flares up again, in time no one will remember when they were made."

sentences.zh: 」京曰：「事苟當於理，多言不足畏也。

translations.literal: " Jing said, "If the matter accords with reason, much talk is not worth fearing."
translations.idiomatic: " Jing said, "If a matter is reasonable, much talk is nothing to fear."

sentences.zh: 陛下當享天下之奉，區區玉器，何足計哉！」

translations.literal: Your Majesty ought to enjoy the tribute of all under Heaven—what are petty jade vessels worth calculating!"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty ought to enjoy the tribute of the realm. Why fuss over a few jade vessels?"

sentences.zh: 五年正月，彗出西方，其長竟天。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year a comet appeared in the west, its tail stretching across the sky.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year a comet appeared in the west with a tail that stretched across the sky.

sentences.zh: 帝以言者毀黨碑，凡其所建置，一切罷之。

translations.literal: Because remonstrators attacked the faction stele, the emperor abolished everything Jing had established.
translations.idiomatic: Because critics attacked the faction stele, the emperor abolished everything Jing had established.

sentences.zh: 京免為開府儀同三司、中太乙宮使。

translations.literal: Jing was removed and made Defender-in-Chief with Three-Duke honors and commissioner of the Central Taiyi Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was dismissed from office and made Defender-in-Chief with Three-Duke honors and commissioner of the Central Taiyi Palace.

sentences.zh: 其党陰援于上，大觀元年，復拜左僕射。

translations.literal: His faction secretly supported him at court; in the first year of Daguan he was again appointed Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: His faction secretly worked on his behalf at court, and in the first year of Daguan he was again appointed Left Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 以南丹納土，躐拜太尉，受八寶，拜太師。

translations.literal: Because Nandan submitted its territory, he was leap-promoted to Grand Commandant, received the Eight Treasures, and appointed Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When Nandan submitted its territory, he was promoted in one leap to Grand Commandant, received the Eight Treasures, and was made Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 三年，台諫交論其惡，遂致仕。

translations.literal: In the third year the censorate and remonstrance officials together discussed his wickedness, and he then retired.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year censors and remonstrators joined in denouncing his crimes, and he retired from office.

sentences.zh: 猶提舉修《哲宗實錄》，改封楚國，朝朔望。

translations.literal: He still superintended compilation of the Veritable Records of Zhezong, changed enfeoffment to Chu, and attended court on the first and fifteenth.
translations.idiomatic: He still supervised compilation of the Veritable Records of Zhezong, was enfeoffed as Duke of Chu, and attended court on the first and fifteenth of each month.

sentences.zh: 太學生陳朝老追疏京惡十四事，曰瀆上帝、罔君父、結奧援、輕爵祿、廣費用、變法度、妄製作、喜導諛、箝台諫、熾親黨、長奔競、崇釋老、窮土木、矜遠略。

translations.literal: The Imperial University student Chen Chaolao submitted a follow-up memorial listing fourteen evils of Jing, saying: blasphemy against the Supreme Lord, deception of ruler and father, forming hidden support, treating titles and salaries lightly, expanding expenditures, changing laws and institutions, reckless creations, delighting in leading flattery, shackling the censorate and remonstrance, inflaming kin factions, encouraging frantic competition, exalting Buddhism and Daoism, exhausting earthworks and timber, and boasting of distant strategies.
translations.idiomatic: The university student Chen Chaolao submitted a follow-up memorial listing fourteen crimes of Jing: blasphemy against Heaven, deceiving ruler and father, building secret patronage networks, treating offices lightly, expanding expenditures, changing laws, reckless innovations, encouraging flattery, silencing remonstrators, inflaming factionalism, encouraging frantic office-seeking, exalting Buddhism and Daoism, exhausting the realm with construction, and boasting of grand foreign campaigns.

sentences.zh: 乞投畀遠方，以禦魑魅。

translations.literal: He begged to cast him to a distant place to guard against demons.
translations.idiomatic: He begged that Jing be cast into a distant place to ward off evil spirits.

sentences.zh: 其書出，士人爭相傳寫，以為實錄。

translations.literal: When his text appeared, scholars vied to copy and transmit it, taking it as a true record.
translations.idiomatic: When the text circulated, scholars copied it eagerly and treated it as an unofficial veritable record.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，彗復出奎、婁間，御史張克公論京輔政八年，權震海內，輕錫予以蠹國用，托爵祿以市私恩，役將作以葺居第，用漕船以運花石。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year the comet again appeared between Kui and Lou; the censor Zhang Kegong discussed how Jing had assisted government for eight years, his authority shaking the realm within the seas, lightly bestowing rewards to ruin state expenditure, relying on titles and salaries to trade private favor, employing the Directorate of Works to repair his residence, and using transport barges to carry fancy stones and flowers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year the comet reappeared between the constellations Kui and Lou. Censor Zhang Kegong charged that during eight years as chief minister Jing's power had shaken the realm, that he squandered state funds with careless rewards, traded offices for private loyalty, used the Directorate of Works to repair his mansion, and commandeered transport barges to ship ornamental stones.

sentences.zh: 名為祝聖而修塔，以壯臨平之山；

translations.literal: In the name of praying for the sage he built a pagoda to strengthen the mountain at Linping;
translations.idiomatic: He built a pagoda in the name of praying for the emperor's longevity to magnify the mountain at Linping;

sentences.zh: 托言灌田而決水，以符「興化」之讖。

translations.literal: under the pretext of irrigating fields he released water to match the omen of "Xinghua."
translations.idiomatic: and under the pretext of irrigating fields he released floodwaters to fulfill the omen embedded in his native place name, Xinghua.

sentences.zh: 法名退送，門號朝京。

translations.literal: His Buddhist name was "Sending Back," and his gate was called "Facing the Capital."
translations.idiomatic: His Buddhist name was "Sending Back," and his gate was called "Facing the Capital."

sentences.zh: 方田擾安業之民，圜土聚徙郡之惡。

translations.literal: The square-field system disturbed people secure in their livelihoods; the round-earth prisons gathered the wicked of relocating prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The square-field survey harassed people secure in their livelihoods, and the round-earth prisons gathered criminals from relocated prefectures.

sentences.zh: 不軌不忠，凡數十事。

translations.literal: Improper and disloyal acts numbered several tens of matters.
translations.idiomatic: His disloyalty and misconduct ran to dozens of charges.

sentences.zh: 先是，御史中丞石公弼、侍御史毛注數劾京，未允，至是，貶太子少保，出居杭。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Censor-in-Chief Shi Gongbi and Attending Censor Mao Zhu had several times impeached Jing without success; at this point he was demoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and sent out to reside in Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the censor-in-chief Shi Gongbi and attending censor Mao Zhu had impeached Jing repeatedly without success. Now he was demoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and sent to live in Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 政和二年，召還京師，復輔政，徙封魯國，三日一至都堂治事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenghe he was recalled to the capital, again assisted government, changed enfeoffment to Lu, and came once every three days to the Metropolitan Secretariat to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenghe he was recalled to the capital, resumed assisting government, was enfeoffed as Duke of Lu, and came to the Metropolitan Secretariat every three days to conduct business.

sentences.zh: 京之去也，中外學官頗有以時政為題策士者。

translations.literal: When Jing departed, school officials inside and outside the capital quite often used current policy as examination topics for candidates.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing left office, many school officials inside and outside the capital set examination topics drawn from current politics.

sentences.zh: 提舉淮西學士蘇棫欲自售，獻議請索五年間策問，校其所詢，以觀向背，於是坐停替者三十餘人。

translations.literal: The Huaidong academic superintendent Su Chou wished to sell himself, submitted a proposal requesting the examination questions of five years, comparing what was asked to observe leanings, and thereby more than thirty persons were punished with suspension.
translations.idiomatic: Su Chou, academic superintendent of Huaidong, sought to curry favor and proposed seizing five years of examination questions to see which candidates had leaned against Jing. More than thirty men lost their posts as a result.

sentences.zh: 初，國制，凡詔令皆中書門下議，而後命學士為之。

translations.literal: At first, by national regulation all edicts were discussed by the Central Secretariat and Chancellery, and only afterward were academics ordered to draft them.
translations.idiomatic: Originally, by state regulation every edict was debated by the Secretariat and Chancellery before an academician was ordered to draft it.

sentences.zh: 至熙寧間，有內降手詔不由中書門下共議，蓋大臣有陰從中而為之者。

translations.literal: By the Xiuning period there were inner descent handwritten edicts not discussed jointly by the Secretariat and Chancellery; probably great ministers secretly acted from within to do this.
translations.idiomatic: By the Xiuning era there were handwritten edicts issued from within the palace that bypassed Secretariat and Chancellery review, probably because powerful ministers were manipulating the process in secret.

sentences.zh: 至京則又患言者議己，故作御筆密進，而丐徽宗親書以降，謂之御筆手詔，違者以違制坐之。

translations.literal: By Jing's time he again feared that remonstrators would discuss him, so he made imperial brush writings secretly submitted and begged Huizong to write them personally before descent, calling them Imperial Brush Handwritten Edicts; violators were punished for violating regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, fearing remonstrance, had secret drafts submitted as imperial brush writings and begged Huizong to copy them out personally. These were called Imperial Brush Handwritten Edicts, and anyone who disobeyed them was punished for violating regulations.

sentences.zh: 事無巨細，皆托而行，至有不類帝劄者，群下皆莫敢言。

translations.literal: Matters great and small were all entrusted through these to be carried out; some even did not resemble the emperor's style, yet the multitude below all did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: Great and small affairs alike were carried out through them, and some did not even sound like the emperor's own writing. No one below dared object.

sentences.zh: 由是貴戚、近臣爭相請求，至使中人楊球代書，號曰「書楊」，京復病之而亦不能止矣。

translations.literal: Thereby noble kin and close ministers vied to request them, even to the point of making the inner attendant Yang Qiu write in substitution, called "Writer Yang"; Jing again resented this yet also could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial relatives and favored ministers then competed to obtain such edicts, even having the inner attendant Yang Qiu write them on their behalf, earning the nickname "Writer Yang." Jing disliked this too but could not stop it.

sentences.zh: 既又更定官名，以僕射為太、少宰，自稱公相，總治三省。

translations.literal: He then again changed official titles, making Vice Directors into Grand and Junior Chancellors, calling himself Duke Chancellor, and governing all three departments in total.
translations.idiomatic: He then revised official titles again, renaming the grand councilors as Grand and Junior Chancellors, styling himself Duke Chancellor, and placing all three departments under his control.

sentences.zh: 追封王安石、蔡確皆為王，省吏不復立額，至五品階以百數，有身兼十餘奉者。

translations.literal: He posthumously enfeoffed Wang Anshi and Cai Que both as kings; provincial clerks no longer established quotas, until fifth-rank grades numbered in the hundreds, and some persons held more than ten salaries at once.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously enfeoffed Wang Anshi and Cai Que as kings. Department clerks no longer kept salary quotas straight, fifth-rank posts ran into the hundreds, and some men held more than ten stipends at once.

sentences.zh: 侍御史黃葆光論之，立竄昭州。

translations.literal: The Attending Censor Huang Baoguang discussed this and was immediately exiled to Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Attending censor Huang Baoguang criticized this and was immediately exiled to Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 拔故吏魏伯芻領榷貨，造料次錢券百萬緡進入，徽宗大喜，持以示左右曰：「此太師與我奉料也。

translations.literal: He promoted his former clerk Wei Bochu to head the Monopoly Bureau, fabricated material-order money certificates of a million strings and presented them; Huizong was greatly pleased, held them up to show those at his side, and said, "This is the Grand Preceptor's provision stipend for me."
translations.idiomatic: He promoted his former clerk Wei Bochu to head the Monopoly Bureau. Wei fabricated commodity money certificates worth a million strings and presented them to the throne. Huizong was delighted, showed them to his attendants, and said, "This is the Grand Preceptor's provision stipend for me."

sentences.zh: 」擢伯芻至徽猷閣待制。

translations.literal: " He promoted Bochu to Huaiyou Hall Attendant Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: " He then promoted Bochu to Attendant Drafter in the Huaiyou Hall.

sentences.zh: 京每為帝言，今泉幣所積贏五千萬，和足以廣樂，富足以備禮，於是鑄九鼎，建明堂，修方澤，立道觀，作《大晟樂》，制定命寶。

translations.literal: Jing often spoke to the emperor, saying that now the accumulated surplus of currency and coin was fifty million; harmony sufficed to broaden music, wealth sufficed to prepare ritual—thereupon he cast the Nine Cauldrons, built the Bright Hall, repaired the Square Mound, established Daoist abbeys, composed the "Great Splendor Music," and fixed the Mandate Treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Jing often told the emperor that the treasury now held a surplus of fifty million strings, enough harmony to expand music, and enough wealth to supply ritual. On that basis he had the Nine Cauldrons cast, the Bright Hall built, the Square Mound repaired, Daoist abbeys established, the "Great Splendor Music" composed, and the Mandate Treasures ordained.

sentences.zh: 任孟昌齡為都水使者，鑿大伾三山，創天成、聖功二橋，大興工役，無慮四十萬。

translations.literal: He appointed Meng Changling Director of Waterways, excavated the three mountains of Dayi, created the Tiancheng and Shenggong bridges, and launched great labor projects involving no less than four hundred thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Meng Changling Director of Waterways, excavated the three mountains of Dayi, built the Tiancheng and Shenggong bridges, and launched vast public works employing some four hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 兩河之民，愁困不聊生，而京僴然自以為稷、契、周、召也。

translations.literal: The people of the two He regions were distressed and could scarcely live, yet Jing complacently regarded himself as Ji, Qi, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the Yellow River valleys were destitute and desperate, yet Jing complacently compared himself to the sage ministers Ji, Qi, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao.

sentences.zh: 又欲廣宮室求上寵媚，召童貫輩五人，風以禁中逼側之狀。

translations.literal: He also wished to expand the palaces to seek the emperor's favor and flattery; he summoned Tong Guan and four others, hinting at how cramped the forbidden precincts were.
translations.idiomatic: He also wanted to enlarge the palaces to win the emperor's favor and summoned Tong Guan and four others, hinting at how cramped the inner palace had become.

sentences.zh: 貫俱聽命，各視力所致，爭以侈麗高廣相誇尚，而延福宮、景龍江之役起，浸淫及于艮嶽矣。

translations.literal: Guan all obeyed orders; each according to his capacity strove to outdo the others in luxury, height, and breadth, and thus the projects at Yanfu Palace and Jinglong River arose, gradually spreading to Genyue as well.
translations.idiomatic: They all obeyed. Each man did what he could and competed to make his projects more lavish, grand, and vast. Work began on Yanfu Palace and the Jinglong River, and eventually the Genyue mound project followed.

sentences.zh: 子攸、儵、翛，攸子行，皆至大學士，視執政。

translations.literal: His sons You, Shu, and Xiu, and You's son Xing, all reached Grand Academician and were regarded like chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: His sons You, Shu, and Xiu, along with You's son Xing, all rose to Grand Academician and were treated like chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 鞗尚茂德帝姬。

translations.literal: Tiao married Princess Maode.
translations.idiomatic: Tiao married Princess Maode of the imperial house.

sentences.zh: 帝七幸其第，賚予無算。

translations.literal: The emperor seven times visited his residence, bestowing rewards beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited his mansion seven times and lavished gifts on him beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 命坐傳觴，略用家人禮。

translations.literal: He was ordered to sit and pass the cup, roughly using family ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He was told to sit and pass the wine cup, in a manner that roughly followed family etiquette.

sentences.zh: 廝養居大官，媵妾封夫人，然公論益不與，帝亦厭薄之。

translations.literal: Servants and grooms held great offices, concubines were enfeoffed as ladies, yet public opinion increasingly rejected him, and the emperor also grew weary and slighted him.
translations.idiomatic: Servants held high office, concubines were ennobled as ladies, public opinion turned ever more against him, and even the emperor grew weary of him.

sentences.zh: 宣和二年，令致仕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuanhe he was ordered to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xuanhe he was ordered to retire from office.

sentences.zh: 六年，以朱勔為地，再起領三省。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, on Zhu Mian's ground, he was again raised to head the three departments.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, with Zhu Mian paving the way, he was brought back to head all three departments.

sentences.zh: 京至是四當國，目昏眊不能事事，悉决于季子絛。

translations.literal: By then Jing had held national power four times; his eyes were dim and he could not handle every matter, and all was decided by his youngest son Tao.
translations.idiomatic: By then Jing had held power four times. His eyes had failed and he could no longer manage affairs himself, so everything was decided by his youngest son Tao.

sentences.zh: 凡京所判，皆絛為之，且代京入奏。

translations.literal: Whatever Jing adjudicated, Tao did it, and moreover entered court in Jing's place to report.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever Jing was supposed to decide, Tao decided for him and even entered court to report in his place.

sentences.zh: 每造朝，侍從以下皆迎揖，呫囁耳語，堂吏數十人，抱案後從，由是恣為奸利，竊弄威柄，驟引其婦兄韓梠为户部侍郎，媒糵密謀，斥逐朝士，創宣和庫式貢司，四方之金帛與府藏之所儲，盡拘括以實之，為天子之私財。

translations.literal: Whenever he came to court, attendants and below all greeted him with bows; he muttered in their ears, and several tens of hall clerks followed behind carrying documents. Thereby he wantonly pursued illicit profit, secretly wielded authority, suddenly promoted his wife's elder brother Han Liu to Vice Minister of Revenue, fomented secret plots, expelled court scholars, created the Xuanhe Treasury Tribute Office, and confiscated gold and silk from all directions and what the state treasuries stored to fill it as the Son of Heaven's private wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he came to court, attendants and lower officials bowed to greet him while he whispered in their ears. Dozens of clerks followed carrying documents. He then pursued illicit profit at will, manipulated power in secret, and abruptly promoted his wife's elder brother Han Liu to Vice Minister of Revenue. Through secret plotting he drove out court officials, created the Xuanhe Treasury Tribute Office, and seized gold, silk, and state reserves from across the realm to fill the emperor's private coffers.

sentences.zh: 宰臣白時中、李邦彥惟奉行文書而已，既不能堪。

translations.literal: The chief ministers Bai Shizhong and Li Bangyan only carried out documents, and could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers Bai Shizhong and Li Bangyan could do nothing but carry out his paperwork, and they could not endure it.

sentences.zh: 兄攸亦發其事，上怒，欲竄之，京力丐免，特勒停侍養，而安置韓梠黄州。

translations.literal: His elder brother You also exposed the matter; the emperor was angry and wished to exile Tao. Jing strenuously begged for exemption; he was specially ordered to suspend attendance and remain in attendance on his father, while Han Liu was assigned to Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother You also exposed the affair. The emperor was furious and wanted to exile Tao, but Jing begged hard for mercy. Tao was ordered to suspend court attendance and remain at home, while Han Liu was banished to Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，褫絛侍讀，毀賜出身敕，而京亦致仕。

translations.literal: Before long Tao was stripped of Lecturer-in-Waiting, his bestowed jinshi origin decree was destroyed, and Jing also retired.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Tao was stripped of his post as imperial reader and his bestowed jinshi decree was revoked. Jing retired as well.

sentences.zh: 方時中等白罷絛以撼京，京殊無去意。

translations.literal: Just as Bai Shizhong and others memorialized to dismiss Tao in order to shake Jing, Jing had no intention of leaving at all.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Shizhong and others had memorialized to dismiss Tao in order to undermine Jing, yet Jing showed no intention of leaving.

sentences.zh: 帝呼童貫使詣京，令上章謝事，貫至，京泣曰：「上何不容京數年，當有相讒譖者。

translations.literal: The emperor called Tong Guan to go to Jing and order him to submit a memorial resigning office. When Guan arrived, Jing wept and said, "Why will Your Majesty not tolerate Jing for several years? There must be someone slandering me."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Tong Guan to tell Jing to submit a resignation memorial. When Guan arrived, Jing wept and said, "Why will Your Majesty not keep me on for a few more years? Someone must be slandering me."

sentences.zh: 」貫曰：「不知也。

translations.literal: " Guan said, "I do not know."
translations.idiomatic: " Guan replied, "I do not know."

sentences.zh: 」京不得已，以章授貫，帝命詞臣代為作三表請去，乃降制從之。

translations.literal: " Jing had no choice but to give the memorial to Guan. The emperor ordered literary officials to draft three memorials requesting departure on his behalf, and then issued an edict accepting it.
translations.idiomatic: " Jing had no choice but to hand the memorial to Guan. The emperor ordered literary officials to draft three resignation memorials for him and then issued an edict accepting his retirement.

sentences.zh: 欽宗即位，邊遽日急，京盡室南下，為自全計。

translations.literal: When Emperor Qinzong ascended, the frontier grew urgent day by day; Jing moved his whole household south as a plan for self-preservation.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Qinzong ascended the throne, the frontier crisis grew daily worse. Jing moved his entire household south in a bid to save himself.

sentences.zh: 天下罪京為六賊之首，侍御史孫覿等始極疏其奸惡，乃以秘書監分司南京，連貶崇信、慶遠軍節度副使，衡州安置，又徙韶、儋二州。

translations.literal: All under Heaven condemned Jing as chief among the Six Traitors; Attending Censor Sun Jue and others first submitted extreme memorials on his treachery and wickedness. He was then made Superintendent of the Palace Library at Nanjing, successively demoted to Vice Military Commissioner of Chongxin and Qingyuan armies, assigned to Hengzhou, and again transferred to Shao and Dan prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The realm condemned Jing as the leader of the Six Traitors. Attending censor Sun Jue and others submitted fierce memorials detailing his crimes. He was made superintendent of the Palace Library at Nanjing, then demoted repeatedly to vice military commissioner of Chongxin and Qingyuan, assigned to Hengzhou, and finally transferred to Shao and Dan.

sentences.zh: 行至潭州死，年八十。

translations.literal: On reaching Tanzhou he died, aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Tanzhou on the way, at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 京天資凶譎，舞智禦人，在人主前，顓狙伺為固位計，始終一說，謂當越拘攣之俗，竭四海九州之力以自奉。

translations.literal: Jing was by nature fierce and treacherous, wielding cleverness to control others. Before the ruler he craftily watched and schemed to secure his position, always with one doctrine: that one ought to transcend restrictive custom and exhaust the strength of all four seas and nine provinces to serve oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was fierce and treacherous by nature, using his wits to manipulate others. Before the throne he schemed constantly to hold his position, always preaching that the court should break free of restrictive custom and exhaust the strength of the entire realm to supply the emperor's pleasures.

sentences.zh: 帝亦知其奸，屢罷屢起，且擇與京不合者執政以柅之。

translations.literal: The emperor also knew his treachery, repeatedly dismissed and repeatedly raised him, and moreover chose those incompatible with Jing to administer government to check him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew he was treacherous, dismissed him repeatedly yet brought him back, and even appointed ministers who opposed Jing to restrain him.

sentences.zh: 京每聞將退免，輒入見祈哀，蒲伏扣頭，無復廉恥。

translations.literal: Whenever Jing heard he was to be dismissed, he would enter audience to beg for mercy, prostrating himself and knocking his head, without any remaining sense of shame.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he heard he was to be dismissed, he rushed into audience to beg for mercy, kowtowing without a trace of shame left.

sentences.zh: 燕山之役，京送攸以詩，陽寓不可之意，冀事不成得以自解。

translations.literal: At the Yan Mountains campaign, Jing sent You a poem outwardly expressing disapproval, hoping the affair would fail so he could excuse himself.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yan Mountains campaign, Jing sent You a poem that outwardly expressed disapproval, hoping the venture would fail so he could distance himself from it.

sentences.zh: 見利忘義，至於兄弟為參、商，父子如秦、越。

translations.literal: Seeing profit he forgot righteousness, to the point that brothers were like Shen and Shang stars, father and sons like Qin and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He forgot righteousness for profit, until brothers were estranged like opposing stars and father and sons were divided like enemy states.

sentences.zh: 暮年即家為府，營進之徒，舉集其門，輸貨僮隸得美官，棄紀綱法度為虛器。

translations.literal: In his later years he made his house into a government office; those seeking advancement all gathered at his gate, presenting goods and slaves to obtain fine offices, and laws and institutions were abandoned as empty vessels.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he turned his house into a private court. Office-seekers flocked to his gate, buying posts with bribes and slaves, while law and institutions became empty forms.

sentences.zh: 患失之心無所不至，根株結盤，牢不可脫。

translations.literal: His fear of losing power reached everywhere; roots and trunks intertwined and could not be pulled loose.
translations.idiomatic: His fear of losing power knew no bounds. His network of patronage was so deeply rooted that it could not be torn out.

sentences.zh: 卒致宗社之禍，雖譴死道路，天下猶以不正典刑為恨。

translations.literal: He finally brought disaster on the altars of state; though punished to death on the road, all under Heaven still resented that he had not received proper statutory punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He ultimately brought disaster on the dynasty. Though he died in exile on the road, the realm still resented that he had never received proper punishment.

sentences.zh: 子八人，儵先死，攸、翛伏誅，絛流白州死，鞗以尚帝姬免竄，余子及諸孫皆分徙遠惡郡。

translations.literal: He had eight sons: Shu died first; You and Xiu were executed; Tao was exiled to Baizhou and died there; Tiao escaped exile because he had married an imperial princess; the remaining sons and all grandsons were separately banished to distant evil prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He had eight sons. Shu died first; You and Xiu were executed; Tao was exiled to Baizhou and died there; Tiao escaped punishment because he had married an imperial princess; the remaining sons and grandsons were banished to remote prefectures.

sentences.zh: 弟 卞

translations.literal: Younger brother Bian
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother: Bian

sentences.zh: 卞字元度，與京同年登科，調江陰主簿。

translations.literal: Bian, styled Yuandu, passed the examination in the same year as Jing and was assigned as Jiangyin registrar.
translations.idiomatic: Bian, whose style name was Yuandu, passed the civil service examination in the same year as Jing and was appointed registrar of Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 王安石妻以女，因從之學。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi married a daughter to him, and he therefore studied under him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi gave him a daughter in marriage, and he studied under Wang as a result.

sentences.zh: 元豐中，張璪薦為國子直講，加集賢校理、崇政殿說書，擢起居舍人，曆同知諫院、侍御史。

translations.literal: During Yuanfeng, Zhang Zuan recommended him as Erudite Lecturer of the Imperial University; he was added as Collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and Lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall, promoted to Attendant Gentleman, and served as Associate Remonstrance Official and Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfeng era Zhang Zuan recommended him as erudite lecturer of the Imperial University. He became collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall, then rose to attendant gentleman and served as associate remonstrance official and attending censor.

sentences.zh: 居職不久，皆以王安石執政親嫌辭。

translations.literal: He did not long remain in office, each time resigning on grounds of kinship with Wang Anshi in power.
translations.idiomatic: He did not remain long in any post, resigning each time on grounds of kinship with Wang Anshi, who was then in power.

sentences.zh: 拜中書舍人兼侍講，進給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Central Secretariat Drafter and concurrent Lecturer, and advanced to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed drafter in the Central Secretariat and concurrent lecturer, then promoted to supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong was installed, he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, he was made Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 使於遼，遼人頗聞其名。

translations.literal: On mission to Liao, the Liao people had quite heard his name.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to the Liao, the Khitan had already heard of his reputation.

sentences.zh: 卞適有寒疾，命載以白馳車，典客者曰：「此，君所乘，蓋異禮也。

translations.literal: Bian happened to have a cold illness and was ordered carried in a white swift carriage; the protocol officer said, "This is what Your Lordship rides—it is an exceptional courtesy."
translations.idiomatic: Bian happened to be ill with a cold and was ordered carried in a white swift carriage. The protocol officer said, "This is the carriage Your Lordship rides—it is an exceptional courtesy."

sentences.zh: 」使還，以龍圖閣待制知宣州，徙江寧府，曆揚、廣、越、潤、陳五州。

translations.literal: " On returning from the mission, he was made Dragon Diagram Hall Attendant Drafter and prefect of Xuanzhou, transferred to Jiangning prefecture, and served in Yang, Guang, Yue, Run, and Chen—five prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: " After returning from his mission he was made attendant drafter in the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Xuanzhou, then transferred to Jiangning and served in Yang, Guang, Yue, Run, and Chen.

sentences.zh: 廣州寶貝叢湊，一無所取。

translations.literal: Guangzhou was crowded with precious goods, yet he took not a single thing.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou was crowded with precious goods, yet he took none of them.

sentences.zh: 及徙越，夷人清其去，以薔薇露灑衣送之。

translations.literal: When he was transferred to Yue, the barbarians cleared his departure and sent him off by sprinkling rose dew on his garments.
translations.idiomatic: When he left for Yue, local tribesmen cleared his path and sprinkled rose dew on his robes as a farewell gift.

sentences.zh: 紹聖元年，復為中書舍人，上疏言：「先帝盛德大業，卓然出千古之上，發揚休光，正在史策。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaosheng he again became Central Secretariat Drafter and submitted a memorial saying, "The late emperor's magnificent virtue and great enterprise stand clearly above a thousand ages; to display his glorious radiance lies precisely in the historical records."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaosheng he again became a Central Secretariat drafter and memorialized, "The late emperor's magnificent virtue and great achievements stand above a thousand ages. To display his glory depends on the historical record."

sentences.zh: 而實錄所紀，類多疑似不根，乞驗索審訂，重行刊定，使後世考觀，無所迷惑。

translations.literal: Yet what the Veritable Records record mostly consists of doubtful and unsubstantiated matters. I beg verification, search, careful revision, and renewed publication so that later ages examining them will not be misled.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Veritable Records contain much that is doubtful and unsubstantiated. I beg that they be examined, revised, and republished so that later ages will not be misled."

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: " The court approved his request.

sentences.zh: 以卞兼國史修撰。

translations.literal: Bian was made concurrent compiler of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: Bian was appointed concurrent compiler of the National History.

sentences.zh: 初，安石且死，悔其所作《日錄》，命從子防焚之，防詭以他書代。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Anshi was near death, he regretted his "Daily Records" and ordered his nephew Fang to burn them; Fang deceitfully substituted other books.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as Wang Anshi lay dying, he regretted his "Daily Records" and ordered his nephew Fang to burn them. Fang deceitfully substituted other books instead.

sentences.zh: 至是，卞即防家取以上，因芟落事實，文飾奸偽，盡改所修實錄、正史，於是呂大防、范祖禹、趙彥若、黃庭堅皆獲深譴。

translations.literal: At this point Bian took them from Fang's house and presented them upward; he then pruned facts, adorned treachery and falsehood, and completely altered the Veritable Records and standard histories he edited. Thereby Lü Dagui, Fan Zuyu, Zhao Yanruo, and Huang Tingjian all received severe condemnation.
translations.idiomatic: Now Bian retrieved them from Fang's house and presented them to the throne. He pruned facts, embellished falsehoods, and rewrote the Veritable Records and standard histories he edited. Lü Dagui, Fan Zuyu, Zhao Yanruo, and Huang Tingjian were all severely punished as a result.

sentences.zh: 遷翰林學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜尚書左丞，專托「紹述」之說，上欺天子，下脅同列。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, relying exclusively on the doctrine of "continuing the legacy," deceiving the Son of Heaven above and coercing his colleagues below.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs. He relied wholly on the slogan of "continuing the legacy," deceiving the emperor above and intimidating his colleagues below.

sentences.zh: 凡中傷善類，皆密疏建白，然後請帝親劄付外行之。

translations.literal: Whatever slander of good men there was, he always submitted secret memorials proposing it, then requested the emperor's personal brush edict to be sent out for execution.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he wanted to destroy a good official, he first submitted a secret memorial and then asked the emperor to issue a personal brush edict for enforcement.

sentences.zh: 章惇雖钜奸，然猶在其術中。

translations.literal: Although Zhang Dun was a great traitor, he was still within Bian's methods.
translations.idiomatic: Even Zhang Dun, great traitor though he was, still fell within Bian's manipulations.

sentences.zh: 惇輕率不思，而卞深阻寡言，論議之際，惇毅然主持，卞或噤不啟齒。

translations.literal: Dun was rash and unreflective, while Bian was deep, obstructive, and sparing of words. At discussions Dun would resolutely take charge, while Bian sometimes kept silent and did not open his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Dun was rash and unthinking, while Bian was secretive and taciturn. In deliberations Dun would speak boldly and take charge, while Bian sometimes remained silent.

sentences.zh: 一時論者以為惇跡易明，卞心難見。

translations.literal: Contemporary commentators thought Dun's tracks were easy to discern, while Bian's heart was hard to see.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries said Dun's actions were easy to see through, but Bian's intentions were hard to discern.

sentences.zh: 徽宗即位，諫官陳瓘、任伯雨、御史龔夬疏其兄弟奸惡，瓘并数卞尊私史以厭宗廟之罪，伯雨言：「卞之惡有過於惇。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong ascended, remonstrance officials Chen Guan and Ren Boyu and censor Gong Fu memorialized on the brothers' treachery and wickedness. Guan also counted Bian's honoring of a private history as a crime offending the ancestral temple. Boyu said, "Bian's wickedness surpasses Dun's."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong ascended the throne, remonstrators Chen Guan and Ren Boyu and censor Gong Fu memorialized against the brothers' crimes. Guan also charged Bian with honoring a private history in a way that offended the ancestral temple. Boyu said, "Bian's wickedness surpasses Dun's."

sentences.zh: 去年封事，數千人皆乞斬惇、卞，公議於此可見矣。

translations.literal: Last year in sealed memorials several thousand men all begged to execute Dun and Bian; public opinion on this can be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Last year thousands of sealed memorials demanded the execution of Dun and Bian. Public opinion could hardly be clearer."

sentences.zh: 」遂陳其大罪有六，曰：「誣罔宣仁聖烈保佑之功，欲行追廢，一也；

translations.literal: " He then set forth six great crimes, saying: "Falsely denying Empress Xuanren Shengle's merit in protecting and preserving the dynasty, wishing to pursue posthumous deposition—first;"
translations.idiomatic: " He then listed six great crimes: "First, falsely denying the merit of Empress Xuanren Shengle and seeking her posthumous deposition;"

sentences.zh: 凡紹聖以來竄逐臣僚，皆卞啟而後行，二也；

translations.literal: all banished officials since Shaosheng were initiated by Bian before being carried out—second;
translations.idiomatic: second, all exiles since the Shaosheng era were proposed by Bian before they were carried out;"

sentences.zh: 宮中厭勝事作，哲宗方疑，未知所處，惇欲召禮法官通議，卞云：'既犯法矣，何用禮法官議？

translations.literal: when palace sorcery affairs arose, Zhezong was just suspicious and did not know how to handle them; Dun wished to summon ritual officials for joint discussion, but Bian said, "Since the law has already been violated, why use ritual officials to discuss?"
translations.idiomatic: third, when palace sorcery cases arose and Zhezong was uncertain what to do, Dun wanted ritual officials consulted, but Bian said, "They have already broken the law. Why consult ritual officials?"

sentences.zh: '皇后以是得罪，三也；

translations.literal: 'The empress was condemned on this account—third;
translations.idiomatic: " The empress was condemned on that account;"

sentences.zh: 編排元祐章牘，萋菲語言，被罪者數千人，議自卞出，四也；

translations.literal: compiling Yuanyou memorials with slanderous language, several thousand persons condemned—the proposal came from Bian—fourth;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, compiling Yuanyou memorials into slanderous indictments that condemned thousands, a plan that came from Bian;"

sentences.zh: 鄒浩以言忤旨，卞激怒哲宗，致之遠謫，又請治其親故送別之罪，五也；

translations.literal: Zou Hao offended the imperial intent with his words; Bian enraged Zhezong and caused his distant exile, and also requested punishment for relatives and friends who saw him off—fifth;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, when Zou Hao offended the throne with his words, Bian enraged Zhezong and had him exiled far away, then sought to punish relatives and friends who saw him off;"

sentences.zh: 蹇序辰建看詳訴理之議，章惇遲疑未應，卞即以二心之言迫之，惇默不敢對，即日置局，士大夫得罪者八百三十家，凡此皆卞謀之而惇行之，六也。

translations.literal: Jian Xuchen proposed the review and appeal bureau; Zhang Dun hesitated and did not respond. Bian immediately used words of divided loyalty to press him; Dun was silent and dared not reply, and that very day the bureau was established. Scholar-officials condemned numbered 830 households. All these were plotted by Bian and carried out by Dun—sixth.
translations.idiomatic: sixth, when Jian Xuchen proposed a review and appeal bureau, Zhang Dun hesitated, but Bian accused him of divided loyalty until Dun dared not answer. The bureau was established that same day, and 830 households of scholar-officials were condemned. All of this was plotted by Bian and carried out by Dun."

sentences.zh: 願亟正典刑，以謝天下。

translations.literal: I wish that statutory punishment be quickly applied to appease all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that proper punishment be applied at once to satisfy the realm."

sentences.zh: 」詔以資政殿學士知江甯府，連貶少府少監、分司池州。

translations.literal: " An edict made him Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and prefect of Jiangning, then successively demoted to Junior Supervisor of the Palace Workshops and superintendent at Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: " He was demoted to academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and prefect of Jiangning, then further to junior supervisor of the Palace Workshops and superintendent at Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 才逾歲，起知大名府，徙揚州，召為中太乙宮使，擢知樞密院。

translations.literal: After just over a year he was raised to govern Daming prefecture, transferred to Yangzhou, summoned as commissioner of the Central Taiyi Palace, and promoted to know the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a year he was recalled to govern Daming, transferred to Yangzhou, summoned as commissioner of the Central Taiyi Palace, and promoted to control the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時京居相位，卞禮辭，不許。

translations.literal: At the time Jing held the chief ministership; Bian declined on grounds of ritual propriety, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was then chief minister. Bian declined the post on grounds of propriety, but was not allowed to refuse.

sentences.zh: 帝謀復湟、鄯，問于卞，卞以王厚、高永年對。

translations.literal: The emperor planned to recover Huang and Shan; he asked Bian, and Bian answered with Wang Hou and Gao Yongnian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor planned to recover Huang and Shan and asked Bian whom to use. Bian recommended Wang Hou and Gao Yongnian.

sentences.zh: 與京合謀，竭府藏以事邊，募商人運糧，不復問其直貴賤。

translations.literal: Together with Jing he plotted, exhausting the treasuries for frontier affairs, recruiting merchants to transport grain without again asking whether the price was high or low.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Jing he exhausted the treasuries for frontier campaigns, hired merchants to transport grain, and no longer asked what price they charged.

sentences.zh: 鄯、廓至斗米錢四千，束芻錢千二百，秦中騷困。

translations.literal: In Shan and Kuo a dou of rice cost four thousand cash, a bundle of fodder twelve hundred; Qin region was disturbed and distressed.
translations.idiomatic: In Shan and Kuo grain reached four thousand cash per dou and fodder twelve hundred per bundle. The Qin region was thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 及取三州，進金紫光祿大夫，永年竟為帳下執去以降。

translations.literal: When the three prefectures were taken, he was advanced to Grand Master of the Golden Girdle and Purple Clarity; Yongnian was finally seized under his command and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When the three prefectures were taken, Bian was promoted to Grand Master of the Golden Girdle and Purple Clarity, but Yongnian was eventually seized under his command and forced to surrender.

sentences.zh: 自是西方交兵，連年不息，追仇任伯雨所言，曲自辦理。

translations.literal: From this the western frontier saw warfare year after year without cease. Pursuing a grudge against what Ren Boyu had said, he twisted matters to justify himself.
translations.idiomatic: From then on fighting on the western frontier continued year after year. Nursing a grudge against Ren Boyu's accusations, he twisted matters to justify himself.

sentences.zh: 至欲會獄證治，諸人坐貶。

translations.literal: He even wished to convene a prison case to verify and punish; many persons were demoted.
translations.idiomatic: He even tried to open a joint trial to prove his case, and many men were demoted as a result.

sentences.zh: 卞居心傾邪，一意以婦公王氏所行為至當。

translations.literal: Bian's heart was perverse and partial; he single-mindedly regarded what his father-in-law the Wang clan had done as supremely correct.
translations.idiomatic: Bian was devious at heart and regarded everything his father-in-law Wang Anshi had done as absolutely correct.

sentences.zh: 兄晚達而位在上，致己不得相，故二府政事時有不合。

translations.literal: His elder brother attained office late yet ranked above him, causing him not to become chief minister; therefore the two departments' policies sometimes did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother had risen late yet ranked above him, preventing Bian from becoming chief minister himself. Their policies in the two departments therefore sometimes clashed.

sentences.zh: 京以中旨用童貫為陝西制置使，卞言不宜用宦者，右丞張康國引李憲故事以對，卞曰：「用憲已非美事，憲猶稍習兵，貫略無所長，異時必誤邊計。

translations.literal: Jing by imperial order from within used Tong Guan as Shaanxi commissioner; Bian said eunuchs should not be used. Right Vice Director Zhang Kangguo cited Li Xian's precedent in reply. Bian said, "Using Xian was already not a fine affair; Xian still somewhat knew warfare. Guan has almost no strengths—in time he will surely ruin frontier plans."
translations.idiomatic: Jing used an inner-court order to appoint Tong Guan Shaanxi commissioner. Bian said eunuchs should not be used. Right Vice Director Zhang Kangguo cited Li Xian as a precedent. Bian replied, "Even Li Xian was a bad choice, and he at least knew something of warfare. Guan has almost no talent and will surely ruin frontier strategy in time."

sentences.zh: 」帝令中書行之。

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered the Secretariat to carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered the Secretariat to proceed anyway.

sentences.zh: 京于帝前詆卞，卞求去，以資政殿大學士知河南。

translations.literal: Jing slandered Bian before the emperor; Bian requested to leave and was made Grand Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and prefect of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Jing slandered Bian before the emperor. Bian asked to resign and was made grand academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and prefect of Henan.

sentences.zh: 妖人張懷素敗，卞素與之遊，謂其道術通神，嘗識孔子、漢高祖，至稱為大士，坐降職。

translations.literal: When the sorcerer Zhang Huai Su failed, Bian had long associated with him, saying his Daoist arts reached the divine and that he had once known Confucius and Emperor Gaozu of Han, even calling them great masters; he was demoted on this account.
translations.idiomatic: When the sorcerer Zhang Huai Su was exposed, it came out that Bian had long associated with him, claiming his arts were divine and that he had known Confucius and Emperor Gaozu of Han, even calling them great masters. Bian was demoted for this.

sentences.zh: 旋加觀文殿學士，拜昭慶軍節度使，入為侍讀，進檢校少保、開府儀同三司，易節鎮東。

translations.literal: Soon he was added as Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature, appointed military commissioner of Zhaoqing Army, entered as Lecturer-in-Waiting, advanced to Junior Guardian with the rank of Defender-in-Chief with Three-Duke honors, and changed to the eastern military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature, military commissioner of Zhaoqing, imperial reader, junior guardian with Three-Duke honors, and then transferred to the eastern commission.

sentences.zh: 政和末，謁歸上塚，道死，年六十。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenghe he requested leave to return and visit his ancestral tomb; he died on the road, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhenghe era he asked leave to return home and visit his ancestral tomb. He died on the road at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，諡曰文正。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Grand Preceptor and the posthumous title Wenzheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Wenzheng, "Correct in Culture."

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，追責為甯國軍節度副使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong ascended, he was posthumously punished as Vice Military Commissioner of Ningguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong ascended the throne, he was posthumously demoted to vice military commissioner of Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 紹興五年，又貶單州團練副使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shaoxing he was again demoted to Vice Training Commissioner of Danzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Shaoxing he was demoted again to vice training commissioner of Danzhou.

sentences.zh: 子 攸

translations.literal: Son You
translations.idiomatic: Son: You

sentences.zh: 崇寧三年，自鴻臚丞賜進士出身，除秘書郎，以直秘閣、集賢殿修撰編修《國朝會要》，二年間至樞密直學士。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongning, from Honglu Assistant he was granted jinshi origin, appointed Secretary Gentleman, and with Direct Secretariat Pavilion and Hanlin Compiler status compiled the "Institutional Essentials of Our Dynasty," reaching Associate Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs within two years.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chongning he was granted jinshi status from his post as Honglu assistant, appointed secretary gentleman, and within two years rose to associate academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs while compiling the "Institutional Essentials of Our Dynasty."

sentences.zh: 京再入相，加龍圖閣學士兼侍讀，詳定《九域圖志》，修《六典》，提舉上清寶箓宫、秘書省兩街道錄院、禮制局。

translations.literal: When Jing again entered as chief minister, he was added as Dragon Diagram Hall Academician and concurrent Lecturer, detailed the "Gazetteer of the Nine Regions," compiled the "Six Canons," and superintended the Shangqing Precious Register Palace, both avenues of the Secretariat and Daoist Registrar Office, and the Ritual Regulations Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing returned to power, You was made Dragon Diagram Hall academician and imperial reader, directed revision of the "Gazetteer of the Nine Regions," supervised compilation of the "Six Canons," and headed the Shangqing Precious Register Palace, the Secretariat's two Daoist registrar offices, and the Ritual Regulations Bureau.

sentences.zh: 道、史官僚合百人，多三館雋遊，而攸用大臣子領袖其間，懵不知學，士論不與。

translations.literal: Daoist and historical bureaucrats together numbered a hundred men, mostly talented travelers from the Three Halls, yet You as a great minister's son led them, ignorant of learning; scholarly opinion did not accept him.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist and historical offices together numbered a hundred men, mostly talented scholars from the Three Halls. Yet You, a great minister's son, led them though he knew nothing of learning, and scholarly opinion rejected him.

sentences.zh: 初置宣和殿，命為大學士，賜球文方團金帶，改淮康軍節度使。

translations.literal: When the Xuanhe Hall was first established, he was appointed Grand Academician, granted a square gold belt with ball pattern, and changed to military commissioner of Huaikang Army.
