translations.idiomatic: When the Xuanhe Hall was first established, he was made Grand Academician, granted a square gold belt with ball pattern, and appointed military commissioner of Huaikang.

sentences.zh: 帝將去京，先逐其党劉昺、劉煥等，使御史中丞王安中劾之。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to remove Jing, he first expelled his faction Liu Bing, Liu Huan, and others, and had Censor-in-Chief Wang Anzhong impeach them.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to dismiss Jing, he first expelled his allies Liu Bing and Liu Huan and had censor-in-chief Wang Anzhong impeach them.

sentences.zh: 攸通籍禁庭，聞其事，亟請間百拜以懇，帝意遂解。

translations.literal: You had access to the forbidden court; hearing the affair, he urgently requested a private audience and bowed a hundred times in plea, and the emperor's intent was thereby relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: You had access to the inner palace. Hearing of the move, he urgently requested a private audience and kowtowed a hundred times in plea until the emperor relented.

sentences.zh: 其後與京權勢日相軋，浮薄者復間之，父子各立門戶，遂為仇敵。

translations.literal: Afterward his power with Jing daily clashed; shallow men again sowed division, father and son each established their own factions, and they became enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward his power clashed daily with Jing's. Shallow men sowed division between them, father and son each built his own faction, and they became enemies.

sentences.zh: 攸別居賜第，嘗詣京，京正與客語，使避之，攸甫入，遽起握父手為胗視狀，曰：「大人脈勢舒緩，體中得無有不適乎？

translations.literal: You lived separately in an imperially granted mansion. Once he visited Jing while Jing was speaking with a guest and had the guest withdraw. You had just entered when Jing abruptly rose, grasped his father's hand as if to feel the pulse, and said, "Father's pulse is relaxed and slow—is there perhaps some discomfort in the body?"
translations.idiomatic: You lived in a separate imperial mansion. Once he visited Jing while Jing was talking with a guest and had the guest withdraw. As soon as You entered, Jing rose abruptly, took his father's hand as if to feel his pulse, and said, "Father, your pulse is calm and slow. Are you feeling unwell?"

sentences.zh: 」京曰：「無之。

translations.literal: " Jing said, "There is none."
translations.idiomatic: " Jing said, "No."

sentences.zh: 」攸曰：「禁中方有公事。

translations.literal: " You said, "There is official business in the forbidden precincts."
translations.idiomatic: " You said, "There is urgent business in the palace."

sentences.zh: 」即辭去。

translations.literal: " He immediately took leave and departed.
translations.idiomatic: " He then left at once.

sentences.zh: 客竊窺見，以問京，京曰：「君固不解此，此兒欲以為吾疾而罷我也。

translations.literal: A guest secretly peeked and saw it, and asked Jing. Jing said: "You truly do not understand this — this boy wishes to make it seem I am ill so as to have me removed from office."
translations.idiomatic: A guest who had been watching in secret asked Jing about it. Jing said, "You do not understand this at all — the boy wants people to think I am sick so he can have me dismissed."

sentences.zh: 」閱數日，京果致仕。

translations.literal: After several days, Jing indeed retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days, Jing did in fact retire.

sentences.zh: 以季弟絛鍾愛于京，數請殺之，帝不許。

translations.literal: Because his youngest brother Tao was greatly favored by Jing, he repeatedly requested that he be killed, but the Emperor would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Because his youngest brother Tao was Jing's favorite, You repeatedly asked that he be killed, but the Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 攸曆開府儀同三司、鎮海軍節度使、少保，進見無時，益用事，與王黼得預宮中秘戲，或侍曲宴，則短衫窄褲，塗抹青紅，雜倡優侏儒，多道市井淫媟謔浪語，以蠱帝心。

translations.literal: You successively held the posts of Commissioner with the Staff Equal to the Three Excellencies, Military Commissioner of the Zhenhai Army, and Junior Guardian. He had access to the Emperor at all hours and wielded power ever more freely. He and Wang Fu were admitted to secret diversions within the palace; when attending informal banquets, they wore short jackets and tight trousers, with their faces painted green and red, mingling with singers, acrobats, and dwarfs, and often uttering obscene, ribald street talk to beguile the Emperor's mind.
translations.idiomatic: You rose through the ranks to Commissioner with the Staff Equal to the Three Excellencies, Military Commissioner of the Zhenhai Army, and Junior Guardian. He could see the Emperor at any hour and grew ever more powerful. He and Wang Fu were let into the palace's private entertainments; at informal banquets they wore short jackets and tight trousers, painted their faces green and red, mixed with singers, acrobats, and dwarfs, and filled the air with lewd street banter meant to bewitch the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 妻宋氏出入禁掖，子行領殿中監，視執政，寵信傾其父。

translations.literal: His wife, Lady Song, came and went within the forbidden quarters; his son Xing held the post of Director of the Palace Domestic Service and was treated like a chief minister — favor and trust surpassed even his father.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Song moved freely in the inner palace; his son Xing headed the Palace Domestic Service and was treated like a chief minister. Favor and trust for them exceeded even what Jing himself enjoyed.

sentences.zh: 帝留意道家者說，攸獨倡為異聞，謂有珠星璧月、跨鳳乘龍、天書雲篆之符，與方士林靈素之徒爭證神變事。

translations.literal: The Emperor took an interest in Daoist teachings, and You alone promoted strange tales, claiming signs such as pearl stars and jade moons, riding phoenixes and mounting dragons, and celestial writs in cloud script; he contended with Daoist masters like Lin Lingsu over matters of divine transformation.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was drawn to Daoist doctrine, and You alone peddled marvels — pearl stars and jade moons, phoenix-riding and dragon-mounting, heavenly books written in cloud script — and debated matters of divine transformation with masters such as Lin Lingsu.

sentences.zh: 於是神霄、玉清之祠遍天下，咎端自攸興矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon temples to the Divine Empyrean and Jade Purity spread throughout the realm — the source of calamity began with You.
translations.idiomatic: Temples to the Divine Empyrean and Jade Purity then sprang up across the empire. The roots of disaster began with You.

sentences.zh: 童貫伐燕，以攸副宣撫，攸童騃不習事。

translations.literal: When Tong Guan campaigned against Yan, You was appointed deputy pacification commissioner; You was childish and foolish and unversed in affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong Guan marched against Yan, You was made deputy pacification commissioner. He was childish, foolish, and knew nothing of statecraft.

sentences.zh: 謂功業可唾手致。

translations.literal: He believed that merit and achievement could be obtained at a snap of the fingers.
translations.idiomatic: He thought glory could be seized as easily as snapping his fingers.

sentences.zh: 入辭之日，二美嬪侍上側，攸指而請曰：「臣成功歸，乞以是賞。

translations.literal: On the day he took leave to depart, two beautiful consorts attended at the Emperor's side. You pointed to them and requested: "When I return in success, I beg that these be my reward."
translations.idiomatic: On the day he departed, two beautiful consorts stood at the Emperor's side. You pointed to them and said, "When I return victorious, I ask that these be my reward."

sentences.zh: 」帝笑而弗責。

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed and did not rebuke him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor laughed and did not reprove him.

sentences.zh: 涿州留守郭藥師擁所部八千人舉涿、易二州降，進攸少傅。

translations.literal: Guo Yaoshi, garrison commander of Zhuozhou, led his eight thousand troops to surrender Zhuo and Yi prefectures; You was promoted to Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yaoshi, garrison commander of Zhuozhou, brought his eight thousand men to surrender Zhuo and Yi prefectures, and You was promoted to Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 王師入燕，進少師，封英國公。

translations.literal: When the imperial army entered Yan, he was promoted to Junior Preceptor and enfeoffed as Duke of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army entered Yan, he was made Junior Preceptor and enfeoffed as Duke of Ying.

sentences.zh: 還，領樞密院。

translations.literal: Upon returning, he headed the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he took charge of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 王黼罷政，帝欲大用攸，既而悔之，但進太保，徙封燕。

translations.literal: When Wang Fu was dismissed from office, the Emperor wished to employ You on a grand scale, but afterward regretted it and only promoted him to Grand Guardian, changing his enfeoffment to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Fu fell from power, the Emperor meant to give You great authority, then changed his mind and only promoted him to Grand Guardian, changing his title to Duke of Yan.

sentences.zh: 帝欲內禪，親書「傳位東宮」字授李邦彥，邦彥卻立不敢承，遂以付攸。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to abdicate in favor of the heir apparent and personally wrote the characters "Transfer the throne to the Eastern Palace," handing them to Li Bangyan. Bangyan stepped back and stood without daring to accept them, and so they were passed to You.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wished to abdicate in favor of the heir apparent and personally wrote the words "Transfer the throne to the Eastern Palace," handing the note to Li Bangyan. Bangyan stepped back and would not take it, so it was passed to You instead.

sentences.zh: 攸退，屬其客給事中吳敏，議遂定。

translations.literal: You withdrew and entrusted the matter to his client, the Supervising Secretary Wu Min, and the plan was settled.
translations.idiomatic: You withdrew and entrusted the matter to his client Wu Min, a Supervising Secretary, and the plan was settled.

sentences.zh: 子 翛

translations.literal: Son: Shu
translations.idiomatic: Son: Shu

sentences.zh: 翛初以恩澤為親衛郎、秘書丞，至保和殿學士。

translations.literal: Shu initially received favor and was appointed Attendant of the Imperial Guard and Secretary; he rose to Academician of the Hall of Preservation and Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Shu first entered office by imperial favor as Attendant of the Imperial Guard and Secretary, and rose to Academician of the Hall of Preservation and Harmony.

sentences.zh: 宣和中，拜禮部尚書兼侍講。

translations.literal: In the Xuanhe era, he was appointed Minister of Rites and concurrently Palace Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xuanhe reign he was appointed Minister of Rites and Palace Lecturer.

sentences.zh: 時翛弟兄亦知事勢日異，其客傅墨卿、孫傅等復語之曰：「天下事必敗，蔡氏必破，當亟為計。

translations.literal: At that time Shu and his brothers also knew that the situation was changing day by day. His clients Fu Moqing, Sun Fu, and others again told him: "Affairs under Heaven will surely fail, the Cai clan will surely be destroyed — you must quickly devise a plan."
translations.idiomatic: By then Shu and his brothers could see that the times were turning against them. His clients Fu Moqing, Sun Fu, and others urged him again: "The empire is doomed to collapse, the Cai clan is doomed to fall — you must act at once."

sentences.zh: 」翛心然之，密與攸議，稍持正論，故與京異。

translations.literal: Shu was convinced in his heart and secretly discussed matters with You, gradually holding to upright views — hence he differed from Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Shu agreed in his heart and secretly consulted with You, gradually taking more upright positions, and so came to differ from Jing.

sentences.zh: 然皆蓄縮不敢明言，遂引吳敏、李綱、李光、楊時等用之，以挽物情。

translations.literal: Yet all were hesitant and dared not speak openly; they therefore brought in Wu Min, Li Gang, Li Guang, Yang Shi, and others to employ them, so as to win over public sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they all shrank back and dared not speak plainly, and so brought in Wu Min, Li Gang, Li Guang, Yang Shi, and others to win back public opinion.

sentences.zh: 尋加大學士，提舉醴泉觀。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Grand Academician and placed in charge of the Shrine of Sweet Springs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Grand Academician and put in charge of the Shrine of Sweet Springs.

sentences.zh: 欽宗立，翛上募兵陝西策，自請行，又勸西幸，帝頗採納，俾知京兆府。

translations.literal: When Emperor Qinzong ascended the throne, Shu submitted a plan to raise troops in Shaanxi, volunteered to go himself, and also urged moving the court westward. The Emperor largely adopted his advice and appointed him to govern the Capital Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Qinzong came to the throne, Shu submitted a plan to raise troops in Shaanxi, asked to lead it himself, and urged the court to move west. The Emperor largely accepted his advice and appointed him governor of the Capital Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 計垂就，攸忌其功成，會金破濬州，徽宗南幸，攸假徽宗旨，請翛守鎮江，改資政殿大學士。

translations.literal: When the plan was nearly complete, You envied him the success and, coinciding with the Jin capture of Junzhou and Emperor Huizong's southern progress, You invoked Huizong's order to request that Shu hold Zhenjiang, changing his title to Grand Academician of the Hall for Aid in Governance.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the plan was nearing success, You, jealous that Shu would win credit, took advantage of the Jin capture of Junzhou and Huizong's flight south. Invoking Huizong's authority, he had Shu posted to guard Zhenjiang and changed his title to Grand Academician of the Hall for Aid in Governance.

sentences.zh: 或謂翛前計已乖，宜勿行。

translations.literal: Some told Shu that his former plan had already gone awry and that he ought not to go.
translations.idiomatic: Some advised Shu that his earlier plan had already failed and that he should not go.

sentences.zh: 翛幸得去，不復辭。

translations.literal: Shu was glad to get away and made no further objection.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was only too glad to leave and raised no objection.

sentences.zh: 流言至京師，謂將復辟於鎮江。

translations.literal: Rumors reached the capital that he would restore Huizong to the throne at Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors reached the capital that he would restore Huizong to power at Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 帝趣迎上皇還，而責翛昭信軍節度副使。

translations.literal: The Emperor urgently ordered Huizong welcomed back and demoted Shu to Vice Military Commissioner of the Zhaoxin Army.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor urgently ordered Huizong brought back and demoted Shu to Vice Military Commissioner of the Zhaoxin Army.

sentences.zh: 攸之誅也，御史陳述且行，帝取詔批其尾曰：「翛亦然。

translations.literal: When You was executed, Censor Chen Shu was about to depart on the edict when the Emperor took the document and wrote at its end: "The same for Shu."
translations.idiomatic: When You was executed, Censor Chen Shu was about to carry out the edict when the Emperor took it and wrote at the end, "The same for Shu."

sentences.zh: 」於是並誅。

translations.literal: Thereupon both were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Both were then executed.

sentences.zh: 族子 崈

translations.literal: Clan nephew: Chong
translations.idiomatic: Clan nephew: Chong

sentences.zh: 崈者，京族子也。

translations.literal: Chong was a clansman of Jing's.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was a clansman of Jing's.

sentences.zh: 性矯妄，善談鬼神事。

translations.literal: By nature he was perverse and arrogant, skilled at discourse on spirits and demons.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was arrogant and eccentric, and skilled at talk of spirits and demons.

sentences.zh: 當承門蔭，固推與庶兄，宗族稱為賢。

translations.literal: When he was due to inherit privilege by family rank, he firmly yielded it to his elder half-brother, and the clan praised him as worthy.
translations.idiomatic: When he was due to inherit office by family privilege, he firmly yielded the place to his elder half-brother, and the clan praised him as virtuous.

sentences.zh: 崇甯初，京黨以學行修飭聞諸朝，與泉州布衣呂注皆著道士服。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chongning era, Jing's faction recommended him to the court for learning and conduct properly cultivated; he and the commoner Lu Zhu of Quanzhou both wore Daoist robes.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Chongning reign, Jing's faction commended him to the court for cultivated learning and conduct. He and the commoner Lu Zhu of Quanzhou both wore Daoist robes.

sentences.zh: 召入謁，累官拜給事中兼侍讀。

translations.literal: Summoned to audience, he rose through successive offices to be appointed Supervising Secretary and concurrently Imperial Reader.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to court, he rose through successive posts until he was appointed Supervising Secretary and Imperial Reader.

sentences.zh: 京去位，為言者所攻，以顯謨閣待制提舉崇福宮。

translations.literal: When Jing left office, he was attacked by critics and was made Gentleman Consultant of the Hall of Manifest Counsel, in charge of the Shrine of Blessings and Prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing left office, critics attacked him, and Chong was made Gentleman Consultant of the Hall of Manifest Counsel and put in charge of the Shrine of Blessings and Prosperity.

sentences.zh: 言者復論其不學無文，結豪民，規厚利，持道家吐納之說以為論思，侍立集英瞑目自若為不恭，遂奪職。

translations.literal: Critics again charged that he was without learning or literary attainment, that he consorted with powerful commoners seeking great profit, that he advanced Daoist breathing exercises as topics for imperial counsel, and that standing attendance in the Hall of Assembled Excellence with eyes closed as if at ease showed disrespect — whereupon his office was stripped from him.
translations.idiomatic: Critics again accused him of being unlearned and uncultured, of consorting with powerful locals for profit, of offering Daoist breathing techniques as counsel to the throne, and of standing in attendance in the Hall of Assembled Excellence with eyes closed as if at ease — conduct deemed disrespectful. His office was then stripped from him.

sentences.zh: 陳正匯上京變事，置獄京師，具陳在杭州時，日聞崈盛言京有後福，獄上，詔削其籍。

translations.literal: Chen Zhenghui submitted the case of Jing's crimes, and a prison was established in the capital. He fully stated that while in Hangzhou he had daily heard Chong lavishly declare that Jing would enjoy later fortune. When the case was submitted, an edict stripped Chong from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhenghui reported Jing's crimes, and a case was opened in the capital. He testified that while in Hangzhou he had daily heard Chong declare at length that Jing would yet enjoy great fortune. When the case was submitted, an edict removed Chong from the official rolls.

sentences.zh: 京復相，徽宗戒毋得用崈但復集英殿修撰，旋還待制，提點洞霄宮。

translations.literal: When Jing again became chief minister, Huizong warned that Chong must not be employed, but restored him as Compiler of the Hall of Assembled Excellence; he soon regained his Gentleman Consultant title and was placed in charge of the Cave of Heaven Abode.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing returned as chief minister, Huizong warned that Chong must not be used, but restored him only as Compiler of the Hall of Assembled Excellence. He soon regained his Gentleman Consultant title and was put in charge of the Cave of Heaven Abode.

sentences.zh: 宣和中，卒。

translations.literal: In the Xuanhe era, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Xuanhe reign.

sentences.zh: 趙良嗣

translations.literal: Zhao Liangsi
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Liangsi

sentences.zh: 趙良嗣，本燕人馬植，世為遼國大族，仕至光祿卿。

translations.literal: Zhao Liangsi was originally Ma Zhi of Yan; his family for generations were a great clan of the Liao state, and he rose in office to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Liangsi was originally Ma Zhi of Yan. His family had for generations been a great clan of the Liao state, and he rose to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 行汙而內亂，不齒於人。

translations.literal: His conduct was filthy and his household disorderly; people would not rank him among decent company.
translations.idiomatic: His conduct was foul and his household chaotic, and respectable people would not associate with him.

sentences.zh: 政和初，童貫出使，道盧溝，植夜見其侍史，自言有滅燕之策，因得謁。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhenghe era, Tong Guan went on a mission and passed by Lugou. Zhi visited his attendant by night, declaring of his own accord that he had a strategy to destroy Yan, and thereby gained an audience.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhenghe reign, Tong Guan went on a mission and passed Lugou Bridge. Zhi visited his attendant by night, saying on his own that he had a plan to destroy Yan, and thereby gained an audience.

sentences.zh: 童貫與語，大奇之，載與歸，易姓名曰李良嗣。

translations.literal: Tong Guan spoke with him and was greatly impressed; he took him back with him and changed his name to Li Liangsi.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Guan spoke with him and was greatly impressed. He brought him back and changed his name to Li Liangsi.

sentences.zh: 薦諸朝，即獻策曰：「女真恨遼人切骨，而天祚荒淫失道。

translations.literal: Recommended to the court, he immediately submitted a plan, saying: "The Jurchens hate the Liao people to the bone, while Tianzuo is dissolute and has lost the Way."
translations.idiomatic: Recommended to court, he at once submitted a plan: "The Jurchens hate the Liao to the bone, while Tianzuo is dissolute and has lost the Way."

sentences.zh: 本朝若遣使自登、萊涉海，結好女真，與之相約攻遼，其國可圖也。

translations.literal: If our dynasty sends envoys from Deng and Lai to cross the sea, befriend the Jurchens, and agree with them to attack Liao jointly, that state can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: If our dynasty sends envoys from Deng and Lai across the sea to befriend the Jurchens and join them in attacking Liao, that state can be taken.

sentences.zh: 」議者謂祖宗以來，雖有此道，以其地接諸蕃，禁商賈舟船不得行，百有餘年矣。

translations.literal: Critics said that since the time of our founding ancestors, although this route existed, because the region bordered various barbarian peoples, merchant ships had been forbidden from traveling it for more than a hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Critics replied that although this route had existed since the time of the founding ancestors, the region bordered foreign peoples and merchant shipping had been forbidden there for more than a hundred years.

sentences.zh: 一旦啟之，懼非中國之利。

translations.literal: To open it in a single day — they feared it would not benefit China.
translations.idiomatic: To reopen it now, they feared, would not serve China's interests.

sentences.zh: 徽宗召見，問所來之因，對曰：「遼國必亡，陛下念舊民遭塗炭之苦，復中國往昔之疆，代天譴責，以治伐亂，王師一出，必壺漿來迎。

translations.literal: Huizong summoned him for audience and asked the reason for his coming. He replied: "The Liao state will surely perish. Your Majesty, taking pity on the old subjects suffering torment, should restore China's former borders, punishing in Heaven's stead, using order to overthrow chaos — when the imperial army sets out, people will surely come bearing soup and wine to welcome it."
translations.idiomatic: Huizong summoned him and asked why he had come. He answered, "The Liao state is doomed to fall. Your Majesty, moved by the suffering of the old subjects, should restore China's former borders, punish evil in Heaven's name, and use order to overthrow chaos. When the imperial army marches forth, the people will surely come out with food and drink to welcome it."

sentences.zh: 萬一女真得志，先發制人，後發制於人，事不侔矣。

translations.literal: Should the Jurchens by any chance prevail, he who strikes first controls others, while he who strikes later is controlled by others — the outcomes would not be comparable.
translations.idiomatic: If by any chance the Jurchens prevail, he who strikes first controls others, while he who strikes later is controlled by others — the outcomes would not be the same.

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉納之，賜姓趙氏，以為秘書丞，圖燕之議自此始。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised and accepted it, granted him the surname Zhao, and appointed him Secretary — from this the plan to take Yan began.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised and accepted the plan, granted him the surname Zhao, and appointed him Secretary. From this the plan to take Yan began.

sentences.zh: 遷直龍圖閣，提點萬壽觀，加右文殿修撰。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Direct Associate of the Dragon Diagram Hall, placed in charge of the Shrine of Ten Thousand Longevities, and made Compiler of the Hall of Right Literature.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Direct Associate of the Dragon Diagram Hall, put in charge of the Shrine of Ten Thousand Longevities, and made Compiler of the Hall of Right Literature.

sentences.zh: 宣和二年二月，使于金國，見其主阿骨打，議取燕、雲。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Xuanhe, he was sent as envoy to the Jin state, met their ruler Aguda, and negotiated the seizure of Yan and Yun.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year of Xuanhe, he was sent as envoy to the Jin state, met their ruler Aguda, and negotiated the recovery of Yan and Yun.

sentences.zh: 使還，進徽猷閣待制。

translations.literal: When the mission returned, he was promoted to Gentleman Consultant of the Hall of Manifest Strategy.
translations.idiomatic: When the mission returned, he was promoted to Gentleman Consultant of the Hall of Manifest Strategy.

sentences.zh: 自是將命至六七，頗能緩頰盡心，與金爭議，進龍圖閣直學士。

translations.literal: From this he bore imperial commissions six or seven times, fairly able to plead patiently and exhaust his effort, arguing with the Jin; he was promoted to Direct Academic of the Dragon Diagram Hall.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he carried out imperial missions six or seven times, pleading earnestly and arguing hard with the Jin. He was promoted to Direct Academic of the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 既得燕山，又加延康殿學士、提舉上清宮，官至光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Once Yanshan was obtained, he was further made Academic of the Hall of Extended Tranquility and placed in charge of the Upper Clarity Palace, rising in office to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yanshan had been taken, he was further made Academic of the Hall of Extended Tranquility and put in charge of the Upper Clarity Palace, rising to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 良嗣言：「頃在北國，與燕中豪士劉范、李奭及族兄柔吉三人結義同心，欲拔幽、薊歸朝，瀝酒於北極祠下，祈天為約，俟他日功成，即掛冠謝事，以表本心，初非取功名而徼富貴也。

translations.literal: Liangsi said: "Not long ago in the northern state, I joined in sworn brotherhood with three men of one heart — the gallant men of Yan, Liu Fan and Li Shang, and my clansman Rouji — intending to wrench You and Ji back to the court. We poured wine at the shrine of the North Pole and prayed Heaven as witness to our covenant: when success came one day, we would at once hang up our caps and resign office, to show our true hearts — we never sought fame and fortune from the start."
translations.idiomatic: Liangsi said, "Not long ago in the northern state I swore brotherhood with three like-minded men — the gallant men of Yan, Liu Fan and Li Shang, and my clansman Rouji — intending to wrest You and Ji back to the court. We poured wine at the shrine of the North Pole and prayed Heaven to witness our oath: when success came one day, we would at once resign and retire, to show our true hearts. We never sought fame or fortune in the first place."

sentences.zh: 賴陛下威靈，今日之事幸而集，顧前日之約豈可欺哉？

translations.literal: Relying on Your Majesty's majesty, today's affair has happily come together — yet how can the covenant of former days be broken?
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to Your Majesty's majesty, today's success has come together — yet how can I break the oath of former days?

sentences.zh: 願許臣致仕，使得買田歸耕，令有識者曰：'此平燕首謀之人，得請閑退，天下美事也。

translations.literal: I beg that I be permitted to retire, that I may buy fields and return to farming, so that men of discernment may say: 'This man who first plotted the pacification of Yan has been granted leisure to withdraw — a fine thing for all under Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: I beg to be allowed to retire, to buy fields and return to farming, so that men of discernment may say, 'The man who first plotted the pacification of Yan has been granted a quiet withdrawal — a fine thing for all under Heaven.'

sentences.zh: '不然，則臣為敢欺神明，何所不至？

translations.literal: 'Otherwise, if your servant dares deceive the spirits, what would I not dare to do?'
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, if your servant dares deceive the spirits, what would I not dare to do?'

sentences.zh: 」凡三上章，詔不許。

translations.literal: In all he submitted three memorials; an edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted three memorials in all, but an edict refused his request.

sentences.zh: 既而朝廷納張覺，良嗣爭之云：「國家新與金國盟，如此必失其歡，後不可悔。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the court accepted Zhang Jue. Liangsi objected, saying: "The state has newly allied with the Jin — if we do this we will surely lose their goodwill, and later we cannot regret it in time."
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the court accepted Zhang Jue. Liangsi objected, saying, "The state has just allied with the Jin. If we do this we will surely lose their goodwill, and later we will not be able to undo it."

sentences.zh: 」不聽。

translations.literal: They did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not listen.

sentences.zh: 坐奪職，削五階。

translations.literal: For this he was stripped of office and reduced five ranks.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was stripped of office and demoted five ranks.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年四月，御史胡舜陟論其結成邊患，敗契丹百年之好，使金寇侵陵，禍及中國，乞戮之於市。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Jingkang, Censor Hu Shunzhi argued that he had created border troubles, destroyed a hundred years of good relations with the Khitans, caused Jin brigands to invade and oppress, and brought calamity upon China — he requested that Liangsi be executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Jingkang, Censor Hu Shunzhi argued that he had created border troubles, ruined a century of good relations with the Khitans, brought Jin invaders down upon the realm, and spread calamity across China. He asked that Liangsi be executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 時已竄郴州，詔廣西轉運副使李升之即所至梟其首，徙妻子于萬安軍。

translations.literal: He had already been banished to Chenzhou. An edict ordered Li Shengzhi, Vice Transport Commissioner of Guangxi, to behead him wherever he was found, and his wife and children were exiled to Wanan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He had already been banished to Chenzhou. An edict ordered Li Shengzhi, Vice Transport Commissioner of Guangxi, to behead him wherever he was found, and his wife and children were exiled to Wanan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 張覺，平州義豐人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Jue was a native of Yifeng in Ping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jue was a native of Yifeng in Ping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 在遼國第進士，為遼興軍節度副使。

translations.literal: He ranked as a presented scholar in the Liao state and served as Vice Military Commissioner of Liaoxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: He had passed the highest examinations in the Liao state and served as Vice Military Commissioner of the Liaoxing Army.

sentences.zh: 鎮民殺其節度使蕭諦裏，覺拊定亂者，州人推領州事。

translations.literal: The townspeople killed their Military Commissioner Xiao Dili. Jue comforted those who had settled the turmoil, and the people of the prefecture urged him to lead prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The townspeople killed their Military Commissioner Xiao Dili. Jue comforted those who had restored order, and the people of the prefecture urged him to take charge of its affairs.

sentences.zh: 燕王淳死，覺知遼必亡，籍丁壯五萬人，馬千匹，練兵為備。

translations.literal: When Prince Chun of Yan died, Jue knew the Liao would surely perish; he registered fifty thousand able-bodied men and a thousand horses and drilled troops in preparation.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Chun of Yan died, Jue knew the Liao was doomed. He registered fifty thousand able-bodied men and a thousand horses and drilled troops in preparation.

sentences.zh: 蕭後遣時立愛來知州，拒弗納。

translations.literal: The Empress Xiao sent Shi Li'ai to govern the prefecture; Jue refused to accept him.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiao sent Shi Li'ai to govern the prefecture, but Jue refused to accept him.

sentences.zh: 金人入燕，訪覺情狀於遼故臣康公弼，公弼言彼何能為，當示以不疑，乃以為臨海軍節度使，任知平州。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens entered Yan, they inquired about Jue's situation from the former Liao minister Kang Gongbi. Gongbi said, "What can he do? We should show him we do not suspect him." Jue was therefore made Military Commissioner of the Linhai Army and charged with governing Ping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens entered Yan, they asked the former Liao minister Kang Gongbi about Jue's situation. Gongbi said, "What can he do? We should show him we do not suspect him." Jue was therefore made Military Commissioner of the Linhai Army and charged with governing Ping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遼相左企弓等將歸東，粘罕欲先遣兵擒覺，公弼曰：「如此是趣之叛也，我請使焉而觀之。

translations.literal: The Liao chancellor Zuo Qigong and others were about to return east. Nianhan wished first to send troops to seize Jue. Gongbi said: "That would only hurry him into rebellion. Let me go as envoy and observe him."
translations.idiomatic: The Liao chancellor Zuo Qigong and others were about to return east. Nianhan wanted first to send troops to seize Jue. Gongbi said, "That would only drive him to rebel. Let me go as envoy and see for myself."

sentences.zh: 」遂往見覺。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went to see Jue.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to see Jue.

sentences.zh: 覺曰：「契丹八路皆陷，今獨平州存，敢有異志？

translations.literal: Jue said: "The Khitan Eight Circuits have all fallen; now Ping Prefecture alone remains — how would I dare harbor a different intent?"
translations.idiomatic: Jue said, "The Khitan Eight Circuits have all fallen; only Ping Prefecture remains. How would I dare harbor a different intent?"

sentences.zh: 所以未釋甲者，防蕭幹耳。

translations.literal: The reason I have not yet laid down my arms is only to guard against Xiao Gan.
translations.idiomatic: The reason I have not yet laid down my arms is only to guard against Xiao Gan."

sentences.zh: 」厚賂公弼使還。

translations.literal: He bribed Gongbi heavily and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: He bribed Gongbi heavily and sent him back.

sentences.zh: 公弼道其語，粘罕信之，升平州為南京，加覺同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Gongbi reported his words; Nianhan believed him, elevated Ping Prefecture to Southern Capital, and made Jue Associate Grand Counselor of the Eastern and Western Bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Gongbi reported his words. Nianhan believed him, elevated Ping Prefecture to Southern Capital, and made Jue Associate Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 企弓、公弼與曹勇義、虞仲文皆東遷。

translations.literal: Qigong, Gongbi, Cao Yongyi, and Yu Zhongwen all migrated eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Qigong, Gongbi, Cao Yongyi, and Yu Zhongwen all moved eastward.

sentences.zh: 時燕民盡徙，流離道路。

translations.literal: At that time the people of Yan were wholly relocated, wandering destitute along the roads.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the people of Yan were being relocated en masse and wandered destitute along the roads.

sentences.zh: 或詣覺訴：「公弼、企弓等不能守燕，致吾民如是。

translations.literal: Some came to Jue to plead: "Gongbi, Qigong, and the rest could not hold Yan and have reduced our people to this."
translations.idiomatic: Some came to Jue to plead, "Gongbi, Qigong, and the rest could not hold Yan and have reduced our people to this."

sentences.zh: 能免我者，非公而誰？

translations.literal: Who but you, sir, can deliver us?
translations.idiomatic: Who but you can deliver us?

sentences.zh: 」覺召僚屬議，皆曰：「近聞天祚復振於松漠，金人所以急趨山西者，畏契丹議其後也。

translations.literal: Jue summoned his staff to consult. All said: "We have lately heard that Tianzuo has revived in Songmo. The reason the Jurchens hurry west toward Shanxi is that they fear the Khitans will strike from behind."
translations.idiomatic: Jue summoned his staff to consult. All said, "We have lately heard that Tianzuo has revived in Songmo. The reason the Jurchens hurry west toward Shanxi is that they fear the Khitans will strike from behind."

sentences.zh: 公能仗大義，迎故主以圖興復，責企弓等之罪而殺之，縱燕人歸燕，南朝宜無不納。

translations.literal: If you, sir, can uphold great righteousness, welcome the former ruler to plan restoration, charge Qigong and the others with their crimes and execute them, and let the people of Yan return to Yan, the Southern Court ought not to refuse acceptance.
translations.idiomatic: If you uphold great righteousness, welcome the former ruler to plan restoration, charge Qigong and the others with their crimes and execute them, and let the people of Yan return to Yan, the Southern Court ought not to refuse them.

sentences.zh: 儻金人西來，內用營、平之兵，外藉南朝之援，何所懼乎？

translations.literal: If the Jurchens come from the west, using the troops of Ying and Ping within and borrowing aid from the Southern Court without — what is there to fear?
translations.idiomatic: If the Jurchens come from the west, using the troops of Ying and Ping within and borrowing aid from the Southern Court without, what is there to fear?

sentences.zh: 」覺又訪于翰林學士李石，亦以為然。

translations.literal: Jue also consulted Hanlin Academician Li Shi, who likewise thought it right.
translations.idiomatic: Jue also consulted Hanlin Academician Li Shi, who agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃殺企弓等四人，復稱保大三年，繪天祚像於廳事，每事告而後行。

translations.literal: Thereupon he killed Qigong and three others, restored the reign title of third year of Bao Da, painted Tianzuo's portrait in the main hall, and reported every matter to it before acting.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he killed Qigong and three others, restored the reign title to the third year of Bao Da, painted Tianzuo's portrait in the main hall, and reported every matter to it before acting.

sentences.zh: 呼父老諭曰：「女真，仇也，豈可從？

translations.literal: He summoned the elders and instructed them: "The Jurchens are our enemies — how can we follow them?"
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the elders and told them, "The Jurchens are our enemies — how can we follow them?"

sentences.zh: 」指其像曰：「此非汝主乎，豈可背？

translations.literal: Pointing to the portrait, he said: "Is this not your lord? How can you betray him?"
translations.idiomatic: Pointing to the portrait, he said, "Is this not your lord? How can you betray him?"

sentences.zh: 當相約以死，必不得已則歸中國。

translations.literal: Let us covenant to die together; if there is no other choice, then return to China.
translations.idiomatic: Let us covenant to die together; if there is no other choice, then return to China.

sentences.zh: 」燕人尚義，皆景從。

translations.literal: The people of Yan valued righteousness and all followed him in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Yan valued righteousness and all followed him in admiration.

sentences.zh: 於是悉遣徙民歸。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent all the relocated people back.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent all the relocated people back.

sentences.zh: 石更名安弼，偕故三司使高党往燕山說王安中曰：「平州自古形勝之區，地方數百里，帶甲十余萬，覺文武全才，若為我用，必能屏翰王室。

translations.literal: Shi changed his name to An Bi and, together with the former Commissioner of the Three Departments Gao Dang, went to Yanshan to persuade Wang Anzhong, saying: "Ping Prefecture has since antiquity been a strategic region — its territory spans several hundred li, with more than a hundred thousand troops under arms. Jue is a man of complete civil and military talent; if we put him to our use, he can surely shield and buttress the royal house."
translations.idiomatic: Shi changed his name to An Bi and, together with the former Commissioner of the Three Departments Gao Dang, went to Yanshan to persuade Wang Anzhong. He said, "Ping Prefecture has since antiquity been a strategic region — its territory spans several hundred li, with more than a hundred thousand troops under arms. Jue is a man of complete civil and military talent. If we put him to our use, he can surely shield and buttress the throne."

sentences.zh: 苟為不然，彼西迎天祚，北通蕭幹，將為吾肘腋患矣。

translations.literal: If that is not done, he may welcome Tianzuo from the west and link with Xiao Gan in the north — he will become a trouble at our very elbow.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not, he may welcome Tianzuo from the west and link with Xiao Gan in the north, and become a trouble at our very elbow.

sentences.zh: 」安中深然之，具奏於朝，願以身任其責，令安弼、党詣京師。

translations.literal: Wang Anzhong deeply agreed, fully reported to the court, wished to bear the responsibility himself, and ordered An Bi and Dang to proceed to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anzhong strongly agreed, reported fully to court, offered to bear the responsibility himself, and ordered An Bi and Dang to proceed to the capital.

sentences.zh: 徽宗以手劄付詹度曰：「本朝與金國通好，信誓甚重，豈當首違？

translations.literal: Huizong handed a personal note to Zhan Du, saying: "Our dynasty and the Jin state are on terms of friendship; our sworn pledge is weighty indeed — how can we be the first to break it?"
translations.idiomatic: Huizong handed a personal note to Zhan Du, saying, "Our dynasty and the Jin state are on terms of friendship, and our sworn pledge is weighty indeed. How can we be the first to break it?"

sentences.zh: 金人昨所以不即討覺者，以兵在關中而覺抗榆關故也。

translations.literal: The reason the Jin yesterday did not at once punish Jue was that their troops were in Guanzhong while Jue resisted at Yuguan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin had not attacked Jue immediately because their troops were tied down in Guanzhong while Jue held Yuguan Pass.

sentences.zh: 今既已東去，他日西來，則覺蕞爾數城，恐未易當。

translations.literal: Now that they have already gone east, if another day they come west, then Jue's paltry few cities will perhaps not be easy to withstand.
translations.idiomatic: Now that they have moved east, if they return west another day, Jue's few small cities may not be easy to defend.

sentences.zh: 為今之計，姑當密示羈縻足矣。

translations.literal: For the present plan, for the moment one should secretly show restraint and control—that is enough.
translations.idiomatic: For now the best policy is quietly to show restraint and keep him on a leash.

sentences.zh: 」而度數誘致之，諷令內附。

translations.literal: " Yet Du repeatedly enticed him and hinted that he should submit inwardly.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet Du repeatedly enticed him and hinted that he should submit to the Song.

sentences.zh: 宣和五年六月，覺遣書至安撫司云：「金虜恃虎狼之強，驅徙燕京富家巨室，止留空城以塞盟誓，緬想大朝，亦非得已。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Xuanhe, Jue sent a letter to the Pacification Commission saying, "The Jin barbarians rely on tiger-and-wolf strength, driving off the wealthy great houses of Yan capital and leaving only empty cities to satisfy the alliance oath. Thinking of the great court, this too was not without cause."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Xuanhe, Jue wrote to the Pacification Commission, "The Jin rely on brute force, driving the wealthy families of Yanjing into exile and leaving only empty cities to satisfy the treaty. When I think of the great court, I know this was not without reason."

sentences.zh: 遺民假道當管，冤痛之聲，盈于衢路。

translations.literal: The remnant people borrowed the road through our jurisdiction; sounds of grievance and pain filled the streets.
translations.idiomatic: Displaced people passed through our territory, and cries of grief filled the roads.

sentences.zh: 州人不忍，僉謂宜抗賊命，以存生靈，使復父母之邦，且為大朝守禦之備，已盡遣其人過界，謹令掌書記張鈞、參謀軍事張敦固詣安撫司聽命。」

translations.literal: The people of the prefecture could not bear it and all said they ought to resist the enemy's command to preserve the living, restore their parents' homeland, and moreover prepare defenses for the great court. They had already sent all such persons across the border, and respectfully ordered Recorder Zhang Jun and Staff Officer Zhang Dun'gu to go to the Pacification Commission to await orders."
translations.idiomatic: The people could not endure it and agreed to resist the enemy, preserve the living, restore their homeland, and prepare defenses for the great court. I have already sent them across the border and respectfully dispatch Recorder Zhang Jun and Staff Officer Zhang Dun'gu to the Pacification Commission for orders."

sentences.zh: 金人聞覺叛，遣闍母國王將三千騎來討，覺帥兵迎拒之于營州，闍母以兵少，不交鋒而退，大書於門，有「今冬復來」之語。

translations.literal: The Jin heard that Jue had rebelled and sent the Prince of Zhamu with three thousand horsemen to attack. Jue led troops to meet and resist them at Yingzhou. Zhamu, because his force was small, did not join battle and withdrew, writing large characters on the gate with the words "We shall return this winter."
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin learned of Jue's rebellion, they sent the Prince of Zhamu with three thousand cavalry to attack. Jue met them at Yingzhou. Zhamu, finding his force too small, withdrew without fighting and wrote on the gate, "We shall return this winter."

sentences.zh: 覺遂妄以大捷聞，朝廷建平州為泰寧軍，拜覺節度使，以安弼、黨、鈞、敦固皆為徽猷閣待制，宣撫司犒以銀絹數萬。

translations.literal: Jue then falsely reported a great victory. The court made Ping Prefecture into Taiping Army, appointed Jue military commissioner, made An Bi, Dang, Jun, and Dun'gu all Huaiyou Hall Attendant Drafters, and the Pacification Commission rewarded them with tens of thousands in silver and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Jue falsely reported a great victory. The court made Ping into Taiping Army, appointed Jue military commissioner, made An Bi, Dang, Jun, and Dun'gu attendants in the Huaiyou Hall, and the Pacification Commission rewarded them with tens of thousands in silver and silk.

sentences.zh: 詔命至，覺喜，遠出迎。

translations.literal: When the edict arrived, Jue rejoiced and went far out to welcome it.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict arrived, Jue rejoiced and went far out to meet it.

sentences.zh: 金人諜知，舉兵來，覺不得返，同其弟挾所被詔敕奔燕。

translations.literal: Jin spies learned of this and raised troops to come. Jue could not return, and together with his younger brother, carrying the edicts he had received, fled to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Jin spies learned of this and marched against him. Jue could not return and fled to Yan with his younger brother, carrying the edicts he had received.

sentences.zh: 母妻先寓營州，為金人所得，弟聞之，亟往降，獻其詔敕。

translations.literal: His mother and wife had first lodged at Yingzhou and were seized by the Jin. When his brother heard, he hurried to surrender and presented the edicts.
translations.idiomatic: His mother and wife had been staying at Yingzhou and were captured by the Jin. Hearing this, his brother hurried to surrender and handed over the edicts.

sentences.zh: 金人圍平州，覺之從弟及侄固守，金人以納叛為責，且求餉糧，凡攻擊數月，州民數千潰圍走，莫肯降。

translations.literal: The Jin besieged Ping Prefecture; Jue's younger cousins and nephews held firm. The Jin charged them with harboring a rebel and also demanded provisions. They attacked for several months; several thousand prefectural people broke the siege and fled, none willing to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin besieged Ping Prefecture while Jue's cousins and nephews held out. The Jin accused them of harboring a rebel and demanded supplies. After months of assault, thousands of townspeople broke out and fled rather than surrender.

sentences.zh: 金人既平二州，始來索覺，王安中諱之。

translations.literal: After the Jin had pacified the two prefectures, they came to demand Jue. Wang Anzhong concealed him.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin pacified the two prefectures, they demanded Jue. Wang Anzhong concealed him.

sentences.zh: 索愈急，乃斬一人貌類者去。

translations.literal: As the demand grew more urgent, he beheaded a man who resembled him and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: As the demand grew more urgent, he beheaded a look-alike and sent the head.

sentences.zh: 金人曰：「此非覺也。

translations.literal: The Jin said, "This is not Jue."
translations.idiomatic: The Jin said, "This is not Jue."

sentences.zh: 覺匿于王宣撫甲仗庫，若不與我，我自以兵取之。

translations.literal: Jue is hidden in Pacification Commissioner Wang's armory. If you do not give him to me, I shall take him myself with troops."
translations.idiomatic: Jue is hidden in Commissioner Wang's armory. If you do not hand him over, I shall take him by force."

sentences.zh: 」安中不得已，引覺出，數其過，使行刑，覺語殊不遜。

translations.literal: " Anzhong had no choice but to bring Jue out, recounted his offenses, and had the execution carried out. Jue's words were extremely insolent.
translations.idiomatic: " Anzhong had no choice but to produce Jue, recite his crimes, and execute him. Jue spoke with shocking insolence.

sentences.zh: 既死，函首送之，燕之降將及常勝軍皆泣下，郭藥師曰：「若來索藥師，當奈何？

translations.literal: After his death they sent his head in a box. Yan's surrendered generals and the Ever-Victorious Army all wept. Guo Yaoshi said, "If they come to demand Yaoshi, what then shall we do?"
translations.idiomatic: After his death they sent his head in a box. Yan's surrendered generals and the Ever-Victorious Army wept. Guo Yaoshi said, "If they come for me next, what then?"

sentences.zh: 」自是解體，金人終用是啟釁雲。

translations.literal: " From this they fell apart, and the Jin ultimately used this to begin provocation.
translations.idiomatic: " From that moment morale collapsed, and the Jin ultimately used the affair to justify war.

sentences.zh: 郭藥師

translations.literal: Guo Yaoshi
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yaoshi

sentences.zh: 郭藥師，渤海鐵州人也。

translations.literal: Guo Yaoshi was a man of Tiezhou in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yaoshi came from Tiezhou in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 遼之將亡，燕王淳募遼東饑民為兵，使之報怨於女真，目曰「怨軍」，藥師為之渠首。

translations.literal: As Liao was about to perish, Prince of Yan Chun recruited hungry people of eastern Liao as troops to let them vent grievance against the Jurchen, calling them the "Grievance Army," and Yaoshi was their leader.
translations.idiomatic: As Liao was collapsing, the Prince of Yan Chun recruited starving people of eastern Liao to strike at the Jurchen, calling them the "Grievance Army." Yaoshi was their leader.

sentences.zh: 明年，其兩營叛，藥師殺叛者羅青。

translations.literal: The next year two of its camps rebelled, and Yaoshi killed the rebel Luo Qing.
translations.idiomatic: The next year two camps rebelled, and Yaoshi killed the rebel leader Luo Qing.

sentences.zh: 都統蕭幹留二千人為四營，以藥師及張令徽、劉舜仁、甄五臣為將。

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief Xiao Gan left two thousand men in four camps, making Yaoshi, Zhang Linghui, Liu Shunren, and Zhen Wuchen generals.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Xiao Gan kept two thousand men in four camps under Yaoshi, Zhang Linghui, Liu Shunren, and Zhen Wuchen.

sentences.zh: 淳建號于燕，改「怨軍」為「常勝軍」，擢藥師至諸衛上將軍、涿州留守。

translations.literal: Chun established his title in Yan, changed the "Grievance Army" to the "Ever-Victorious Army," and promoted Yaoshi to General-in-Chief of the Guards and garrison commander of Zhuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chun declared himself ruler in Yan, renamed the Grievance Army the Ever-Victorious Army, and promoted Yaoshi to general-in-chief of the guards and garrison commander of Zhuozhou.

sentences.zh: 淳死，蕭後立，蕭幹專，國人貳。

translations.literal: When Chun died, Empress Xiao was installed, Xiao Gan monopolized power, and the people of the state were divided in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: After Chun died, Empress Xiao took power, Xiao Gan dominated the court, and the realm grew disloyal.

sentences.zh: 宣和四年九月，藥師擁所部八千人奉涿、易二州來歸，詔以為恩州觀察使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Xuanhe, Yaoshi led his eight thousand men to bring Zhuo and Yi prefectures in submission; he was appointed Observation Commissioner of Enzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Xuanhe, Yaoshi brought his eight thousand men and the prefectures of Zhuo and Yi in submission. He was appointed observation commissioner of Enzhou.

sentences.zh: 王師北討，劉延慶與幹軍于盧溝，藥師曰：「幹以全師抗我，燕城必虛，選勁騎襲之，可得也。

translations.literal: When the imperial army marched north, Liu Yanqing faced Gan's army at Lugou. Yaoshi said, "Gan is using his whole force to resist us; Yan city must be empty. Choose crack cavalry to strike it and it can be taken."
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army marched north, Liu Yanqing faced Gan at Lugou. Yaoshi said, "Gan has committed his whole army to us, so Yan must be empty. Send crack cavalry in a surprise strike and we can take it."

sentences.zh: 」延慶遣藥師與諸將帥兵六千，夜半渡河，倍道而進。

translations.literal: " Yanqing sent Yaoshi and the generals with six thousand troops, crossing the river at midnight and advancing by double marches.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanqing sent Yaoshi and other generals with six thousand men. They crossed the river at midnight and marched at forced pace.

sentences.zh: 質明，甄五臣領五千騎奪迎春門以入，大軍繼至，下令納燕人降而盡殺契丹雜虜。

translations.literal: At dawn Zhen Wuchen led five thousand cavalry to seize the Yingchun Gate and enter; the main army followed, ordering acceptance of Yan people's surrender while slaughtering all Khitan and mixed barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Zhen Wuchen led five thousand cavalry through the Yingchun Gate. The main army followed with orders to accept Yan submissions but slaughter all Khitan and other barbarians.

sentences.zh: 藥師遣人諭蕭後，使趣降，後密詔蕭幹還戰於三市，藥師失馬，幾為所擒，遂以敗還，猶進安遠軍承宣使。

translations.literal: Yaoshi sent men to urge Empress Xiao to hurry in surrender. She secretly ordered Xiao Gan to return and fight at the Three Markets. Yaoshi lost his horse and was nearly captured, then returned in defeat, yet was still promoted to Pacification Commissioner of Anyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoshi urged Empress Xiao to surrender quickly. She secretly ordered Xiao Gan back to fight at the Three Markets. Yaoshi lost his horse and was nearly captured, then retreated in defeat, yet was still promoted to pacification commissioner of Anyuan.

sentences.zh: 十二月，拜武泰軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was appointed military commissioner of Wutai Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was appointed military commissioner of Wutai.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，加檢校少保，同知燕山府。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year he was added as Junior Guardian with the rank and made Associate Prefect of Yanshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year he was made junior guardian with the rank and associate prefect of Yanshan.

sentences.zh: 詔入朝，徽宗禮遇甚厚，賜以甲第姬妾。

translations.literal: He was ordered to enter court; Huizong treated him with great courtesy and bestowed a fine mansion and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court. Huizong treated him with exceptional honor and gave him a fine mansion and concubines.

sentences.zh: 張水嬉于金明池，使觀之，命貴戚大臣更互設宴。

translations.literal: He spread water sports at the Jinming Pool and had him watch, ordering noble kin and great ministers to take turns hosting banquets.
translations.idiomatic: He staged water games at the Jinming Pool for him to watch and ordered nobles and ministers to host banquets in turn.

sentences.zh: 又召對於後苑延春殿，藥師拜廷下，泣言：「臣在虜，聞趙皇如在天上，不謂今日得望龍顏。

translations.literal: He again summoned him for audience in the Yanchun Hall of the rear garden. Yaoshi bowed below the hall and wept, saying, "Your servant was among the barbarians and heard that the Zhao emperor was like one in Heaven; I did not expect today to behold the dragon countenance."
translations.idiomatic: He summoned him again to the Yanchun Hall in the rear garden. Yaoshi kowtowed and wept, saying, "When I was among the barbarians, I heard the Song emperor was like a god in Heaven. I never expected to see your face today."

sentences.zh: 」帝深褒稱之，委以守燕，對曰：「願效死。

translations.literal: " The emperor greatly praised him and entrusted him to guard Yan. He replied, "I wish to exhaust myself unto death."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor praised him warmly and entrusted Yan to him. He replied, "I am willing to die in your service."

sentences.zh: 」又令取天祚以絕燕人之望，變色而言曰：「天祚，臣故主也，國破出走，臣是以降。

translations.literal: " He also ordered him to capture Tianzuo to cut off the Yan people's hopes. Yaoshi changed color and said, "Tianzuo is your servant's former lord. When the state was broken he fled, and therefore your servant surrendered."
translations.idiomatic: " He also ordered him to capture Tianzuo to destroy Yan hopes of restoration. Yaoshi's face changed and he said, "Tianzuo was my former lord. When the state fell he fled, and that is why I surrendered."

sentences.zh: 陛下使臣畢命他所，不敢辭，若使反故主，非所以事陛下，願以付他人。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty orders your servant to exhaust his life elsewhere, I dare not refuse; but if you make me turn against my former lord, that is not how to serve Your Majesty. I beg you give it to another."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty orders me to die elsewhere, I dare not refuse. But to make me turn against my former lord is not how I should serve you. Please give the task to someone else."

sentences.zh: 」因涕泣如雨。

translations.literal: " He then wept tears like rain.
translations.idiomatic: " He wept profusely.

sentences.zh: 帝以為忠，解所禦珠袍及二金盆以賜。

translations.literal: The emperor regarded this as loyalty, removed his own pearl robe and two gold basins, and bestowed them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took this as loyalty, removed his own pearl robe and two gold basins, and gave them to him.

sentences.zh: 藥師出，諭其下曰：「此非吾功，汝輩力也。

translations.literal: When Yaoshi went out, he told his subordinates, "This is not my merit—it is your strength."
translations.idiomatic: When Yaoshi left, he told his men, "This honor is not mine alone. It is yours."

sentences.zh: 」即剪盆分給之。

translations.literal: " He at once cut up the basins and distributed them.
translations.idiomatic: " He immediately cut up the basins and distributed the pieces among them.

sentences.zh: 加檢校少傅，歸鎮。

translations.literal: He was added as Junior Tutor with the rank and returned to his command.
translations.idiomatic: He was made junior tutor with the rank and returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 蕭干犯塞，藥師破其眾於峰山，生擒阿魯太師，獲耶律德光尊號寶劍檢、塗金印，幹尋為部下所殺。

translations.literal: Xiao Gan violated the frontier; Yaoshi defeated his force at Feng Mountain, captured Alu Taishi alive, and obtained the precious sword tally and gilded seal of the honorific title of Emperor Taizong of the Liao. Gan was soon killed by his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Gan raided the frontier, Yaoshi defeated him at Feng Mountain, captured Alu Taishi alive, and seized the sword tally and gilded seal bearing the honorific title of Emperor Taizong of Liao. Gan was soon killed by his own men.

sentences.zh: 策勳加檢校太傅。

translations.literal: For his merit he was added as Grand Tutor with the rank.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made grand tutor with the rank.

sentences.zh: 初，王安中知燕山府，詹度與藥師同知，藥師自以節鉞，欲居度上。

translations.literal: At first Wang Anzhong governed Yanshan prefecture; Zhan Du and Yaoshi were associate prefects. Yaoshi, considering himself a military commissioner, wished to rank above Du.
translations.idiomatic: At first Wang Anzhong governed Yanshan, with Zhan Du and Yaoshi as associate prefects. Yaoshi, holding a military commission, wanted precedence over Du.

sentences.zh: 度稱御筆所書有序，藥師不從。

translations.literal: Du said the imperial brush writing had an order, but Yaoshi would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Du cited an order in the emperor's own brush writing, but Yaoshi refused to obey.

sentences.zh: 加以常勝軍肆橫，藥師右之，度不能制，告於朝廷。

translations.literal: Moreover the Ever-Victorious Army ran wild; Yaoshi supported them, and Du could not control them, so he reported to court.
translations.idiomatic: The Ever-Victorious Army also ran wild with Yaoshi's support, and Du could not control them, so he reported to court.

sentences.zh: 慮其交惡，命度與河間蔡靖兩易。

translations.literal: Fearing they would become mutually hostile, the court ordered Du and Cai Jing of Hejian to exchange posts.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing open conflict, the court swapped Du with Cai Jing of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 靖至，坦懷待之，藥師亦重靖，稍為抑損，安中但諂事之，朝廷亦曲徇其意，所請無不從。

translations.literal: When Jing arrived, he treated him openly; Yaoshi also respected Jing and somewhat restrained himself. Anzhong only flattered and served him, and the court also bent to his wishes—whatever he requested was not refused.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing arrived he treated Yaoshi openly, and Yaoshi respected him and restrained himself somewhat. Anzhong only flattered him, and the court indulged his every request.

sentences.zh: 良械精甲，多遣部曲貿易他道，為奇巧之物以奉權貴宦侍，於是譽言日聞。

translations.literal: He stockpiled fine armor and often sent retainers to trade on other routes, making ingenious curiosities to present to powerful nobles and eunuch attendants, and thus praise of him was daily heard.
translations.idiomatic: He stockpiled fine armor, sent retainers to trade along other routes, and presented ingenious curios to powerful nobles and eunuchs, so praise of him spread daily at court.

sentences.zh: 專制一路，增募兵號三十萬，而不改左衽，朝論頗以為慮。

translations.literal: He monopolized control of the whole circuit, increased recruitment to a force said to be three hundred thousand, yet did not change left-lapel dress; court opinion was quite concerned.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled the circuit as his own domain, raised his force to a claimed three hundred thousand men, and still dressed in the Jurchen style. Court opinion grew alarmed.

sentences.zh: 亟拜太尉，召入朝，辭不至。

translations.literal: He was soon appointed Grand Commandant and summoned to court, but declined and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Grand Commandant and summoned to court, but refused to come.

sentences.zh: 帝令童貫行邊，陰察其去就，不然，則挾之偕來。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Tong Guan to tour the frontier and secretly observe whether he would stay or go; if not, then bring him along by force.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Tong Guan to tour the frontier and secretly observe his intentions, or if necessary bring him back by force.

sentences.zh: 貫至燕，藥師迎于易州，再拜帳下，貫避之，曰：「汝今為太尉，位視二府，與我等耳，此禮何為？

translations.literal: When Guan reached Yan, Yaoshi welcomed him at Yizhou and bowed twice below his tent. Guan avoided it and said, "You are now Grand Commandant, your rank equal to the Two Departments, the same as us—why this ceremony?"
translations.idiomatic: When Guan reached Yan, Yaoshi welcomed him at Yizhou and bowed twice before his tent. Guan stepped aside and said, "You are Grand Commandant now, equal in rank to us. Why this ceremony?"

sentences.zh: 」藥師曰：「太師，父也。

translations.literal: " Yaoshi said, "Grand Preceptor is a father."
translations.idiomatic: " Yaoshi replied, "Grand Preceptor, you are like a father to me."

sentences.zh: 藥師唯拜我父，焉知其他？

translations.literal: Yaoshi bows only to my father—how would I know anything else?"
translations.idiomatic: I bow only to my father. What do I know of anything else?"

sentences.zh: 」貫釋然。

translations.literal: " Guan was relieved.
translations.idiomatic: " Guan was appeased.

sentences.zh: 遂邀貫視師，至於迥野，略無人跡，藥師下馬，當貫前掉旗一揮，俄頃，四山鐵騎耀日，莫測其數。

translations.literal: He then invited Guan to review the army. They reached open wilds with scarcely a human trace. Yaoshi dismounted and, before Guan, shook a banner once; in a moment iron cavalry on four mountains blazed in the sun, their number beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: He then invited Guan to review his troops in open country where no one else was in sight. Yaoshi dismounted and waved a banner before him. In an instant iron cavalry blazed on four mountains, beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 貫眾皆失色。

translations.literal: Guan and all his party changed color.
translations.idiomatic: Guan and his party were stunned.

sentences.zh: 歸為帝言，藥師必能抗虜，蔡攸亦從中力主之。

translations.literal: On returning he told the emperor that Yaoshi could surely resist the barbarians, and Cai You also strongly supported this from within.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he told the emperor that Yaoshi could surely resist the barbarians, and Cai You strongly backed him from within.

sentences.zh: 金使賀天寧節歸，送伴使見藥師兵，遇之于道，金使為之斂馬引避。

translations.literal: A Jin envoy returning from congratulating the Tianning Festival was seen by the escort commissioner encountering Yaoshi's troops on the road; the Jin envoy reined in his horse and drew aside for them.
translations.idiomatic: A Jin envoy returning from the Tianning Festival saw Yaoshi's troops on the road and reined in his horse to give way.

sentences.zh: 鄉兵或持矛揭取其羊羜，皆不敢爭，奏言藥師威聲遠振，攸益謂其可倚，故內地不復防制。

translations.literal: Local soldiers sometimes took spears and snatched their sheep and carts, yet none dared dispute it. Memorials said Yaoshi's awesome reputation shook far lands; You increasingly said he could be relied on, and therefore the interior was no longer guarded against him.
translations.idiomatic: Local soldiers sometimes seized their sheep and carts with spears, yet none dared resist. Memorials praised Yaoshi's far-reaching reputation. You increasingly argued he could be trusted, and the interior ceased guarding against him.

sentences.zh: 屢有告變及得其通金國書，輒不省。

translations.literal: There were repeatedly reports of rebellion and recovered letters communicating with the Jin state, yet the court would not investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated reports of rebellion and intercepted letters to the Jin were ignored.

sentences.zh: 七年十二月，詹度言：「藥師瞻視不常，趣向懷異，蜂目烏喙，怙寵恃功，逆節已萌，兇橫日甚。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the seventh year Zhan Du said, "Yaoshi's gaze is inconstant, his inclinations harbor difference, his eyes are like a wasp's and his beak like a crow's. Relying on favor and presuming on merit, rebellious intent has already sprouted and fierce insolence grows daily."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the seventh year Zhan Du memorialized, "Yaoshi's gaze is unsettled and his intentions suspect. With wasp eyes and a crow's beak, he relies on favor and merit. Rebellion is already budding and his violence grows daily."

sentences.zh: 今聞與金人交結，背負朝廷，興禍不遠，願早為之慮。

translations.literal: Now I hear he is in league with the Jin, turning his back on the court. Disaster is not far off—I wish an early plan may be made."
translations.idiomatic: I now hear he is in league with the Jin and has turned against the court. Disaster is near. I beg the court to act early."

sentences.zh: 」始詔遣官究實，而金兵已南下破檀、薊，至玉田。

translations.literal: " An edict was first issued to send officials to investigate the facts, but Jin troops had already marched south, broken Tan and Ji, and reached Yutian.
translations.idiomatic: " The court finally ordered an investigation, but Jin troops had already marched south, taken Tan and Ji, and reached Yutian.

sentences.zh: 蔡靖遣藥師、張令徽、劉舜仁帥師出禦，其夕，令徽遁歸，靖與部使者詣藥師計事，藥師欲降，靖曰：「靖誓死報國，此何言邪？

translations.literal: Cai Jing sent Yaoshi, Zhang Linghui, and Liu Shunren to lead troops out to resist. That evening Linghui fled back. Jing and the departmental envoys went to Yaoshi to plan affairs. Yaoshi wished to surrender. Jing said, "Jing swears to die for the state—what words are these?"
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing sent Yaoshi, Zhang Linghui, and Liu Shunren to resist the invaders. That evening Linghui fled. Jing and the envoys went to consult Yaoshi, who wished to surrender. Jing said, "I have sworn to die for the state. What talk is this?"

sentences.zh: 」引佩刀將自剄，藥師抱持之，並諸使者悉鎖于家。

translations.literal: " He drew his girdle dagger to cut his own throat. Yaoshi embraced and held him, and all the envoys were locked in his house.
translations.idiomatic: " He drew his dagger to kill himself. Yaoshi seized him and locked all the envoys in his house.

sentences.zh: 斡離不及郊，藥師率軍官迎拜，遂從以南。

translations.literal: Wolibu reached the suburbs; Yaoshi led military officers out to welcome and bow, then followed him south.
translations.idiomatic: When Wolibu reached the suburbs, Yaoshi led his officers out to welcome him and then followed him south.

sentences.zh: 叛報至，帝猶秘其事，議封為燕王，割地與之，使世守，而已無及。

translations.literal: When word of the rebellion arrived, the emperor still kept the matter secret and discussed enfeoffing him as Prince of Yan and ceding territory for him to hold in perpetuity—but it was already too late.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the betrayal arrived, the emperor still kept it secret and discussed making him Prince of Yan with hereditary territory—but it was already too late.

sentences.zh: 斡離不至慶源，聞天子內禪，欲回軍，藥師曰：「南朝未必有備，不如姑行。

translations.literal: When Wolibu reached Qingyuan and heard the Son of Heaven had abdicated within, he wished to turn the army back. Yaoshi said, "The Southern Court may not yet be prepared—better for the moment to advance."
translations.idiomatic: When Wolibu reached Qingyuan and heard the emperor had abdicated, he wanted to turn back. Yaoshi said, "The Southern Court may not be ready. Better to press on for now."

sentences.zh: 」其後趑趄京城，詰索宮省與邀取寶器服玩，皆藥師導之也。

translations.literal: " Afterward, hesitating before the capital, demanding and seeking the palace offices and seizing precious vessels and ornaments—all were guided by Yaoshi.
translations.idiomatic: " Afterward, as the Jin hesitated before the capital, demanded palace offices, and seized precious vessels and ornaments, Yaoshi guided them in everything.
